nb1fcd5c2db7d: Platelets are anucleate megakaryocyte-derived cytoplastic fragments best known for their roles in hemostasis and thrombosis, but they also play roles in systemic immune surveillance, vascular integrity, and tissue homeostasis. In cancer, this versatility is co-opted through communication between the tumor, bone marrow, and platelets. Tumor-derived cytokines, extracellular vesicles, and inflammatory cues can rewire thrombopoiesis and platelet activation, lifespan, and cargo, giving rise to tumor-educated platelets. Platelets support multiple stages of cancer progression by promoting metastatic traits in the tumor, cancer cell survival in the circulation, immune evasion, and vascular adhesion. Clinically, platelets are key drivers of coagulopathies in cancer patients, including venous and arterial thromboembolism, thrombotic microangiopathy, and disseminated intravascular coagulation. Here, we review platelet biology at the intersection of hemostasis, inflammation, and cancer.
n1a295b636e19: Third culture kids (TCKs) grow up as temporary migrants in a host country with an expectation of repatriation to the home country. Ideologies of being international and interstitial, rather than part of the home or host country cultures, lead to complex identity formation. The continual mobility of community members in expatriate communities results in a superdiverse linguistic feature pool for young TCKs to draw from in their own speech development. Studies have shown TCKs are agentive in their individualized combinations of these features, and they have an advantage over non-TCKs in their perceptual skills across multiple linguistic varieties. During repatriation, TCKs typically acquire the dialect of their home country more quickly and completely than second dialect acquisition studies predict, due to their perceptual exposure to the home country variety from their parents, or due to their previous use of the variety prior to moving to the host country.
nc20436628db1: Meningiomas are the most common primary intracranial tumors, accounting for 42.6% of all central nervous system tumors. Although many meningiomas are indolent, clinical behavior is highly heterogeneous, with recurrence occurring in a minority of low-risk tumors but in more than half of clinically high-risk cases despite standard therapy. During the past decade, significant advancements in molecular profiling have provided insights into meningioma biology and have begun to influence clinical practice. Genomic sequencing, DNA methylation profiling, and gene expression analyses have revealed distinct molecular subgroups with prognostic and therapeutic implications. These advancements, coupled with a growing understanding of the meningioma immune microenvironment, have expanded therapeutic possibilities beyond traditional surgery and radiation approaches. Here, we review how molecular profiling is refining patient stratification and treatment selection, examine the evidence supporting various therapeutic approaches, and explore ongoing clinical trials. Finally, we highlight the critical challenges in advancing personalized medicine for meningioma patients. This comprehensive review provides an integrated overview of current diagnostic and treatment paradigms while offering perspectives on future directions in meningioma therapy.
n130182b473a7: Gastrointestinal smooth muscle cells (SMCs) generate the forces that drive digestion while continuously sensing and adapting to mechanical deformation. How SMCs detect force and convert it into localized chemical and electrical signals remains poorly understood. We propose that mechanosensory output depends on the spatial organization of the nanodomain a channel occupies, and not on the intrinsic properties of that channel alone. Within these environments, mechanosensitive channels integrate opposing depolarizing and hyperpolarizing currents, translating mechanical load into contraction, relaxation, mechanical compliance, or adaptive remodeling. This junction does not appear to be a permanent structure, because it is assembled during development, maintained under load, and eventually lost with age. Which of those elements fails may then determine the clinical phenotype that results. Two questions remain unresolved within this framework: whether stretch reorganizes the nanodomain itself and whether force is also sensed at organelle membranes rather than at the cell surface alone. Emerging tools may finally resolve these dynamics within the active syncytium, uncovering targets for treating dysmotility.
nb1142bc39ba8: Participatory budgeting (PB) is a deliberative decision-making process that invites community participation to direct spending for a defined portion of public budgets. Originating in Brazil in the 1980s, PB has since diffused across the globe, including several hundred cases in the United States and Canada alone. PB programs vary but are generally characterized by five core principles: voice, vote, social inclusion, social justice, and oversight. Research on PB shows promising though moderate associations with improved population health outcomes, including infant mortality reductions and health and sanitation spending increases. Despite PB's conceptual alignment with many public health values, adoption of PB by US public health agencies remains limited, constrained by categorical funding requirements, small discretionary budgets, and a polarized sociopolitical environment. This article reviews PB's conceptual foundations, evidence base, and real-world applications before examining structural and political challenges and opportunities for PB as a means to improve the public's health.

Vilaplana Grosso Objectives To compare soft palate (SP) length, thickness, and volume in French bulldogs and English bulldogs before and after staphylectomy or folded flap palatoplasty (FFP), and to compare the success of procedures in reducing these dimensions. Materials and Methods Dogs diagnosed with brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome (BOAS) underwent staphylectomy (n = 8) or FFP (n = 8). Pre-operative and 4-week post-operative computed tomography was performed to assess SP dimensions and evaluate surgical outcomes. Results Both procedures resulted in a reduction of SP length (staphylectomy mean reduction = 0.91 cm, 95% CI [0.44 cm, 1.39 cm]; FFP mean reduction = 0.86 cm, 95% CI [0.39 cm, 1.33 cm]), and volume (staphylectomy mean reduction = 2.81 cm3, 95% CI [1.36 cm3, 4.27 cm3]; FFP mean reduction = 2.54 cm3, 95% CI [0.84 cm3, 4.24 cm3]) when comparing pre- and post-operative dimensions within each procedure group. Staphylectomy did not result in SP thinning, while FFP resulted in a mean thinning of 0.30 cm (95% CI [0.10 cm, 0.50 cm]). There was no difference in the degree of SP shortening (adjusted mean difference 0.01 cm, 95% CI [−0.33 cm, 0.35] cm) or reduction of SP volume (adjusted mean difference 0.32 cm3, 95% CI [−0.52 cm3, 1.16 cm3]) between procedure groups. Folded flap palatoplasty resulted in greater SP thinning than staphylectomy. Clinical Significance Both staphylectomy and FFP resulted in a reduction of length and volume of the SP. FFP resulted in SP thinning, while staphylectomy did not. In dogs with concurrent SP thickening and elongation, FFP may be the preferred surgical treatment.
n872a03639ca7: Background Emphysema is a significant public health issue. Physical activity (PA) has been suggested to be associated with respiratory health; however, the relationship between PA intensity and emphysema remains insufficiently characterized. Methods This cross-sectional study utilized data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) from 2007 to 2016. Emphysema was defined based on self-reported physician diagnosis. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to examine the association between different levels of PA and the odds of self-reported emphysema among older adults, adjusting for demographic characteristics, lifestyle factors, and comorbidities. Results Higher levels of physical activity, particularly ≥3000 MET-minutes per week, were associated with lower odds of self-reported emphysema. A dose–response relationship was observed, with increasing PA levels associated with progressively lower odds of self-reported emphysema. Conclusions Higher physical activity levels were associated with lower odds of self-reported emphysema in this cross-sectional analysis. These findings highlight a potential association between PA and self-reported emphysema; however, causal inference cannot be established. Prospective studies are warranted to further evaluate this relationship and explore underlying mechanisms.
n1524e26bc942: Early detection of iron deficiency during pregnancy and the postpartum period, a common condition associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, remains challenging with conventional iron markers. Reticulocyte hemoglobin indices, including reticulocyte hemoglobin equivalent and reticulocyte hemoglobin content, may enable earlier detection of iron-restricted erythropoiesis. We conducted a scoping review to map the clinical and research applications of these indices in pregnant and postpartum women. Following Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidance, we searched PubMed, CENTRAL, Web of Science, and Ichushi Web for studies published from January 1, 1990, to May 31, 2025, and performed an updated search on April 21, 2026, for newly added or indexed records. Eligible studies involved pregnant women or women within 3 months postpartum in whom reticulocyte hemoglobin indices were evaluated for clinical or research purposes. We also constructed an evidence map to visualize the distribution of evidence and research gaps. Thirty-five studies were included. Evidence was most developed for diagnostic accuracy for iron deficiency and associations with iron-related biomarkers. Reticulocyte hemoglobin indices generally showed good diagnostic performance, although reported cut-off values varied widely across studies. Data from mid-to-late pregnancy remained limited. Studies using reticulocyte hemoglobin indices as indicators of response to iron therapy are increasing. Some studies examined longitudinal changes and reference values across pregnancy and the postpartum period; however, these studies were methodologically limited. Three studies examined associations between maternal reticulocyte hemoglobin indices and neonatal parameters, whereas no study evaluated maternal clinical outcomes. Overall, reticulocyte hemoglobin indices appear promising for assessing iron status and monitoring response to iron therapy in perinatal populations. However, substantial heterogeneity in study design, reference standards, and analytical platforms, together with limited longitudinal and outcome-oriented evidence, currently constrains broader clinical implementation.
