Espino, Chun-Ho Park, Satoshi Inoue Rabies remains a major public health concern in endemic settings, where effective control depends on timely and reliable post-mortem confirmation of infection in animal reservoirs. Although the direct fluorescent antibody test (dFAT) remains the reference standard, its dependence on fresh brain tissue and susceptibility to specimen degradation limits its operational use in decentralized surveillance systems. The present findings demonstrate that the locally optimized RT-qPCR assay targeting the nucleoprotein gene in non-brain tissues exhibits high analytical sensitivity and strong concordance with dFAT results obtained from post-mortem brain specimens of dogs. The consistent performance in nasal planum and follicle-sinus complex samples supports using safer, more accessible post-mortem specimens, reinforcing the potential for scalable, field-adapted molecular diagnostics to strengthen routine animal rabies surveillance in endemic regions.
nf2de04b8129f: Background A whole school approach (WSA) to physical activity is a comprehensive strategy encouraging children's physical activity throughout the school day. However, research on implementing this approach in special educational needs (SEN) school settings is limited. A strategic approach that considers the school context, behaviour change mechanisms and implementation strategies can improve the effectiveness and sustainability of physical activity in a WSA. This study aimed to embed implementation and behavioural science principles to co-develop an implementation research logic model (IRLM) to guide implementation of a WSA to physical activity in SEN settings. Methods A collaborative co-development approach was used in this study exploring the WSA to physical activity in SEN settings. Teachers, school leadership, parents, the education authority and professionals from community sports clubs in one UK region participated in a series of workshops. The workshops and analyses were guided by behavioural and implementation theories, models, and frameworks. Results Workshop discussions revealed 31 determinants of implementation, comprising 18 facilitators, 12 barriers and one item identified as both barrier and facilitator. These determinants informed the development of eight implementation strategies to promote physical activity through a WSA in SEN settings (e.g., staff training, building collaborative networks and engaging families). Eleven implementation, seven school-level and six pupil-level outcomes, were identified to assess effectiveness and implementation. Eight causal mechanisms explained the pathway from strategies to outcomes. Finally, these determinants, implementation strategies, mechanisms, and outcomes were mapped onto an IRLM to guide the implementation of a WSA to physical activity for children and young people with SENs across settings. Conclusions We have co-developed an IRLM embedded in implementation and behavioural science to support the implementation of a WSA to physical activity in SEN settings. The model illustrates causal mechanisms between implementation determinants and implementation strategies to achieve intended outcomes. This IRLM has informed a guidance document for implementing WSA to physical activity within SEN settings, addressing real-world challenges faced in promoting physical activity among pupils with SEN.
n77b14786e09a: by Angela V. Fonseca-Benitez, David Diaz-Baez, Giulia Capella, Milena Rondón-Lagos, Isabella Castellano, Nelson Rangel Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains the most aggressive breast cancer subtype, with the poorest prognosis among all forms of breast cancer. FOXA1 is a well-known pioneer factor in luminal breast cancer, however, despite its vital role in this tumor subtype, detailed information about FOXA1 expression and function in TNBC is notably lacking. This gap highlights the importance of exploring whether FOXA1 plays different roles across breast cancer subtypes. Accordingly, the present study aimed to assess the independent prognostic value of FOXA1 expression in a well-characterized cohort of 283 women with TNBC, evaluating its association with progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and distant metastasis, and to determine whether this association is independent of the systemic treatment received. Initial analyses employed chi-square and t-tests to identify associations, followed by multivariate logistic and Cox regression models to determine independent predictors. Survival analyses were performed using Kaplan-Meier curves, with comparisons made using the log-rank test. The median age of patients was 69 years. FOXA1 positivity was significantly associated with grade II tumors (p < 0.001) and Ki-67 levels lower than 20% (p < 0.001). In multivariate analysis, FOXA1 was shown to be a poor prognostic factor for PFS (HRa = 1.68; 95% CI: 1.13–2.48; p = 0.009). Furthermore, in treatment-adjusted models, FOXA1 expression remained as an independent predictor of poor PFS (HRa = 1.96; 95% CI: 1.29–2.98; p = 0.001). These findings establish FOXA1 as an independent prognostic biomarker for disease progression in TNBC, with its adverse impact on PFS persisting regardless of the chemotherapeutic regimen administered.
n2a03a333276d: Objectives To evaluate the feasibility of a contrast-only computed tomography angiography (CTA) protocol versus a conventional multiphase protocol for detecting and characterizing acute aortic pathologies, and reducing radiation dose. Materials & methods This retrospective study included 160 patients who underwent multiphase CTA for evaluating acute aortic syndrome. Two readers independently evaluated 640 predefined aortic segments for the presence of aneurysms, dissections, intramural hematomas (IMH), and penetrating atherosclerotic ulcers (PAU). Non-inferiority was assessed using generalized estimating equations with a prespecified 5% margin. Inter-protocol and inter-reader agreements were calculated using Cohen’s kappa. Radiation dose also was compared. Results The contrast-only protocol demonstrated non-inferiority to the full protocol for detecting all major aortic pathologies, with all confidence intervals falling within the 5% margin. Detection rates were identical for aneurysms (33.6% vs. 33.6%; p = 1.000) and similar for dissections (15.6% vs. 15.9%; p = 0.500). Detection rates were slightly higher with the contrast-only protocol for IMH (5.8% vs. 5.0%) and PAU (5.8% vs. 4.7%), primarily reflecting false-positive interpretation. Interprotocol agreement was perfect for aneurysm shape and rupture status (kappa = 1.000) but lower for mural thrombus characterization (kappa = 0.703). The contrast-only protocol achieved a 32.1 ± 5.7% reduction in mean DLP and 32.4 ± 4.5% for CTDI vol (both, p < 0.001). Conclusion In patients with acute aortic pathology, a contrast-only protocol demonstrated non-inferior diagnostic performance to the full multiphase protocol, with comparable reader agreement and a 32% reduction in radiation dose. These findings suggest that omitting the unenhanced phase may be feasible in selected clinical scenarios, particularly in patients undergoing serial surveillance imaging, where cumulative dose reduction is a priority.
nf4866c562ee9: by Erik-Jan A. Haan, Annet Doomen, Harriët Wittink, Henri Kiers, Remco M. Arensman, Caroline B. Terwee Introduction Patient-Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs) are widely used in physical therapy, but both clinicians and patients report respondent burden due to the number and the length of existing instruments. PROMIS® Computerized Adaptive Tests (CATs) may reduce this burden, yet their feasibility in primary care physical therapy is unknown. This study examined the feasibility of Dutch-Flemish PROMIS CATs in patients with musculoskeletal (MSK) disorders of the spine and upper extremity. Methods We conducted a mixed-methods concurrent triangulation study in 14 physical therapy practices where PROMIS CATs were integrated into the electronic health record system and administered during routine care. A survey assessed physical therapists’ experiences and opinions regarding acceptability, demand, practicality, and implementation. Semi-structured interviews with physical therapists and patients further explored these domains. Survey data were analyzed descriptively, and interview transcripts were thematically analyzed by two independent researchers. Results Twenty-five physical therapists completed the survey. Ten physical therapists and nine patients participated in interviews. Most physical therapists reported that PROMIS CATs were easy to use and facilitated focused discussions about symptoms and functioning. Patients described CATs as quick to complete and relevant to their condition and were willing to complete PROMs if results were used in consultations. Reported barriers included the simultaneous use of legacy PROMs (patients), difficulties using the online portal, and uncertainty about interpreting CAT scores (therapists). Some participants reported that certain CAT items felt less relevant and expressed a desire to view individual item responses. Conclusions PROMIS CATs are considered feasible to implement in physical therapy practice and are generally experienced as acceptable, efficient, and clinically useful. Future implementation should focus on phasing out legacy PROMs to reduce respondent burden, improving skills in score interpretation, ensuring financial reimbursement for use, incorporating PROMIS into clinical guidelines, and evaluating additional PROMIS domains relevant to primary care physical therapy.
n528cf1aa6224: The purpose of this article is to study the relationships among the BCI-algebraic class, the GB-algebraic class, and the class of algebras of type (2,0). The results indicate that: (1) The BCH-algebraic class and the GB-algebraic class are two distinct algebraic classes, both of which contain the BCI-algebraic class. (2) There exist a proper BCH-algebra and a proper GB-algebra, and necessary and sufficient conditions are provided for BCH-algebras and GB-algebras to be proper BCH-algebras and proper GB-algebras, respectively. (3) All (2,0)-type algebras form a proper class, and the GB-algebraic class is a proper subclass of the class of algebras of type (2,0). Several conditions for (2,0)-type algebras to be GB-algebras are given.
nb8b83e4d140c: This study examines GenAI-enabled accounting information systems competence (GAISC) among accounting and auditing students and its relationships with GenAI readiness (GAR), perceived ease of use (PEOU), digital learning self-efficacy (DLSE), facilitating conditions (FC), perceived usefulness (PU), AI ethics awareness (AIEA), and career readiness (CR). The model is anchored in Socio-Technical Systems Theory (STS) and Social Cognitive Career Theory (SCCT), with technology readiness, TAM, self-efficacy, and facilitating-condition logic used as construct-level underpinning mechanisms. Survey data from 471 students at five Vietnamese universities were analyzed using PLS-SEM, complemented by a common latent factor diagnostic and Gaussian copula endogeneity assessment. The baseline PLS-SEM model showed statistically significant positive associations for all nine hypothesized relationships and explained 53.1% of the variance in GAISC, 45.6% in AIEA, and 52.9% in CR. Substantively, PU was the strongest baseline antecedent of GAISC (β = .427, f2 = .244), while GAISC showed a particularly strong association with AIEA (β = .675, f2 = .838). Endogeneity adjustment indicated that seven relationships remained robust; however, the relationships between FC and GAISC and between AIEA and CR became non-significant. Accordingly, these two paths are interpreted as baseline-supported but not robust after adjustment. The findings move beyond generic GenAI acceptance by positioning GAISC as an accounting-specific competence construct linked to ethical awareness and career readiness. Because GAISC and CR were measured through student self-reports and the evidence is cross-sectional, the results are interpreted as association-based rather than as demonstrations of objectively verified competence, employability, or causal effects.
na43c9a0e556f: Qat (Catha edulis), chewed daily by a substantial proportion of Yemeni adults, contains cathinone, an amphetamine-like alkaloid that augments masticatory muscle activity. Observational evidence links the habit to temporomandibular disorders (TMD), yet none has examined how chewers respond once treated. A prospective cohort of 148 consecutive patients diagnosed by Research Diagnostic Criteria for Temporomandibular Disorders Axis I examination was followed at Sana’a University and Al-Kuwait Teaching Hospital between October 2018 and October 2020. Fifty-four (36.5%) were habitual qat chewers, defined as three or more sessions weekly. All received reassurance, education and self-care advice, to which the clinician added an NSAID, diazepam, amitriptyline or a stabilization splint as routine care. The outcome was a patient-reported global rating of change at three months, dichotomized as improved or not improved; every patient attended that visit. Improvement occurred in 47 of 54 chewers (87.0%) and 88 of 94 non-chewers (93.6%), a difference of 6.6 percentage points (95% CI −16.8 to 3.7; Fisher exact p = 0.23). The crude odds ratio for improvement among chewers was 0.47 (95% CI 0.15–1.42); it reached 0.92 (95% CI 0.26–3.29) once age and sex were entered, chewers being older and age the only consistent predictor of non-improvement. Treatment components did not differ between groups. Pain presented differently in chewers rather than simply more severely: 29.6% reported none and 24.1% severe pain, none falling in the mild band, so the bands differed in shape (p < 0.001) but not in rank (p = 0.22). Among those in pain, 38 of 40 chewers rated it moderate or severe against 52 of 82 non-chewers. Conservative management benefited nine patients in ten. Powered only for a difference of 16 percentage points or more, the study cannot exclude a clinically meaningful disadvantage to chewers; all adjusted estimates rest on 13 events and are hypothesis-generating.
n0da42a51c1e5: by John V. Dzimianski, Spencer R. Pierce, Sara M. O’Rourke, Ian Kunkel, Kevin Delgado-Cunningham, Aaron D. Gingerich, Jarrod J. Mousa, Ted M. Ross, Rebecca M. DuBois Protein subunit and mRNA vaccines encoding viral glycoprotein antigens fused to the bacteriophage T4 fibritintrimerization domain are increasingly being tested in human clinical trials. AREXVY and ABRYSVO®, subunit vaccines composed of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prefusion F glycoprotein(s) fused to Foldon, are now FDA-approved and regularly administered. However, administration of vaccine antigens containing the Foldon domain has the potential to elicit off-target antibody responses. Here, we demonstrate that protein subunit vaccine antigens RSV F Foldon and influenza hemagglutinin (HA) Foldon elicit antibodies against the Foldon domain. To dampen Foldon-induced antibody responses, we engineered influenza computationally optimized broadly reactive antigen (COBRA) HA proteins with N-glycosylation motif mutations at three different sites in Foldon. Mass spectrometry analyses confirmed partial occupancy of N-glycosylation modifications at two of the three intended sites. Two of the three COBRA HA Foldon mutant antigens demonstrated reduced binding by anti-Foldon monoclonal and polyclonal antibodies compared to the wild-type COBRA HA Foldon. However, mice immunized with the COBRA HA Foldon mutant antigens did not have a significant reduction in the elicitation of anti-Foldon antibodies. Further analysis suggested that some of the observed differences in antibody binding to mutant Foldon antigens can be attributed to differences in protein sequence alone. Altogether, these data suggest that while the N-glycosylation modifications may partially shield the Foldon from reactive antibodies, this shielding does not significantly reduce its immunogenicity in a naïve setting. Importantly, these data highlight that the Foldon trimerization domain is immunogenic, which should be considered during clinical trials of vaccines that contain Foldon.
nd3c328983fa2: Psidium guajava (L.) is a medicinal plant rich in bioactive phytochemicals with promising therapeutic potential. This study aimed to isolate clerodane-type diterpenes from P. guajava and evaluate their anticancer activity through in vitro and in vivo assays supported by molecular docking.Two clerodane-type diterpenes, borapetoside F (1) and borapetoside B (2), were isolated from the ethyl acetate fraction of P. guajava and identified by 1H and 13C NMR spectroscopy. Cytotoxicity was evaluated against Ehrlich Ascites Carcinoma (EAC) cells using the MTT assay and in EAC-bearing Swiss albino mice, with bleomycin as the reference drug. Apoptosis was assessed by microscopy, DNA fragmentation, gene expression analysis. Compounds 1 and 2 demonstrated significant in vitro cytotoxicity, inhibiting EAC cell growth by 82.4% and 79.8%, respectively. In in vivo cytotoxicity assays, these compounds suppressed EAC cell proliferation by 61.26% and 48.88%, respectively. Optical and fluorescence microscopy revealed characteristic apoptotic morphological changes, while DNA fragmentation analysis confirmed apoptosis induction. Gene expression analysis demonstrated upregulation of the pro-apoptotic markers p53, Bax, and Cytochrome C, accompanied by downregulation of the anti-apoptotic genes Bcl-2 and NF-κB. Molecular docking further supported the experimental findings by demonstrating favorable interactions of both compounds with apoptosis-related target proteins. Collectively,. Borapetoside F (1) and borapetoside B (2) exhibit significant anticancer activity by inhibiting EAC cell proliferation and inducing apoptosis, suggesting their potential as promising lead compounds for anticancer drug development.
nee62041a1298: Background Mepolizumab improves control and reduces clinically significant exacerbations in severe asthma patients. Further research is needed to understand factors influencing patient response. Objective Identify predictors of response to mepolizumab using machine learning techniques. Methods Thirty clinically relevant features from the REALITI-A dataset were analyzed. Response to mepolizumab was defined as change in clinically significant exacerbations at Year 1 post-exposure, being free from clinically significant exacerbations at Year 1, and being free from clinically significant exacerbations at both Year 1 and Year 2 post-exposure for primary, secondary, and exploratory analyses, respectively. Linear/logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost models were tested. The best-performing model based on R2 or classification accuracy was used for feature selection. A SHapley Additive exPlanations post-hoc analysis was conducted. Results The primary and secondary analyses included 685 patients; the exploratory analysis included 529 patients. Using XGBoost for the primary analysis, higher pre-exposure clinically significant exacerbations rate, lower body mass index, total immunoglobulin E, lower baseline activity impairment, and lower baseline Asthma Control Questionnaire-5 score were top predictors. For the secondary analysis, the random forest model identified lower pre-exposure clinically significant exacerbations rate, residency outside the United Kingdom, and lower baseline Asthma Control Questionnaire-5 score, body mass index, and baseline activity impairment as top predictors. For the exploratory analysis, XGBoost identified residency outside the United Kingdom, and lower pre-exposure clinically significant exacerbations rate, baseline Asthma Control Questionnaire-5 score, eosinophil levels, and body mass index as top predictors. Conclusion Machine learning models identified key predictors of response to mepolizumab, which could guide clinical decision-making and improve patient outcomes in severe asthma patients.
n144f815f3637: Portable radiography in orthopedic wards exposes healthcare professionals and adjacent patients to scatter radiation in open, shared clinical environments. In crowded wards, maintaining an optimal distance or clearing the area during exposure is often impractical. This study designed, constructed, and evaluated a foldable mobile radiation shielding system comprising two three-panel units, each with a chromed steel frame (210 × 180 cm) with 0.6-mm nominal lead sheets covered by a vinyl outer layer (66 × 100 cm) per panel, mounted on wheeled castors for bedside deployment. The two units were deployed together, one along each lateral side of the bed. Scatter dose rates were measured using an radiation survey meter and a portable X-ray unit during phantom radiography across common orthopedic projections at eight angular positions (0°–315° in 45° increments) and five distances (50–250 cm). The two-unit configuration achieved a median scatter dose reduction of 94.1% (IQR: 88.0%–97.7%; Wilcoxon W = 51,360, N = 320, p < 0.001). Reductions were broadly consistent across tube voltages (65–85 kVp) and remained substantial across all measurement distances (84.3%–89.6% across 50–250 cm), but varied significantly by angular position, with the highest reduction at 90° (mean 96.91%) and the lowest reductions recorded at 0° (mean 54.02%) and 180° (mean 75.69%). These two directions represented the open axial ends of the setup and were not directly covered by the side-mounted shielding panels. Under a representative high-workload scenario, the two-unit configuration reduced estimated annual occupational doses across all projections, with all post-shielding means remaining well below the average annual occupational dose limit of 20 mSv/year. User feedback was more favorable among radiologic technologists (mean 4.80/5) than among orthopedic ward nurses (mean 3.67/5). The two-unit configuration showed substantial scatter reduction and may serve as an additional protective measure during portable radiography in orthopedic ward settings, with positioning guidance required to maximize protection at clinically relevant angular locations.
n3e0a44b65238: Background Mindfulness-based cognitive therapy (MBCT) is an effective treatment for recurrent depression in the general population and is recommended in clinical guidelines for those with mild-moderate depression. However, the effectiveness of MBCT in people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS) with mild to moderate depression is unknown. Further, how best to tailor and implement MBCT for PwMS is largely unstudied. This manuscript describes the study protocol for a hybrid-effectiveness study to evaluate online MBCT tailored for PwMS. Methods This type 1 hybrid effectiveness-implementation study will employ an embedded mixed methods experimental design. Quantitative findings will be collected through a powered waitlist randomized controlled trial examining online MBCT in a minimum of 152 PwMS with case-ness of mild-moderate depression (Clinical Trials Gov #NCT07742579). The intervention will consist of an online 8-week MBCT course with weekly sessions conducted by qualified mindfulness instructors experienced int the care of PwMS. Questionnaires will be collected at baseline, post-intervention, and 3 months later. The primary outcome will be depression, measured using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Score – Depression (HADS-D). An intention-to-treat analysis will be conducted. Qualitative findings will be collected through semi-structured interviews with 30–40 MBCT participants, HCPs, MBCT instructors, and MS decision makers. Thematic analyses will be used to analyze interview data. The RE-AIM PRISM tool will be used to evaluate implementation and mixed data assessed in a joint display. Conclusion The results from this study will provide evidence regarding the effectiveness of online MBCT in PwMS with mild to moderate depression, recommendations for intervention tailoring and implementation. Findings will be disseminated through traditional and novel, creative knowledge mobilization methods.
n33200ac85521: The spatio-Temporal adaptive collaborative logistics network optimization problems investigated in this paper involve multiple objectives. Most evolutionary multi-objective optimization algorithms, however, do not account for the heterogeneity in evaluation times. Instead, they perform high-fidelity evaluations on all objectives for promising population positions identified by their associated surrogate-assisted optimization algorithms in the solution space. While this approach provides complete and error-free solution evaluations, it does not yield the most computationally efficient procedure. To address this limitation, we propose a novel Surrogate-assisted Evolutionary Multi-objective Grey Wolf Optimizer with Probabilistic Ranking Strategy (SAE-MOGWO-PRS). This algorithm is designed to determine which individuals and objective functions within the population should undergo high-fidelity evaluation, thereby enhancing their ability to generate non-dominated solutions with improved convergence and diversity in the Multi-objective Grey Wolf Optimizer. To validate the efficacy of the proposed SAE-MOGWO-PRS algorithm, we compared it against four state-of-the-art surrogate-assisted multi-objective optimization algorithms, including those that specifically handle heterogeneous evaluation times. The comparative analysis on four test problems demonstrates the superior performance of the proposed probabilistic ranking strategy-based algorithm, thereby confirming the effectiveness of the SAE-MOGWO-PRS method.
nd73ac9045bf2: This paper presents a single-layer circularly polarized (CP) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna with wideband operation and high-gain radiation characteristics. The antenna comprises 16 truncated-corner patches arranged in a 4×4 configuration and capacitively excited by a probe-fed rectangular patch, enabling a low-profile single-layer structure. The final two-port MIMO antenna has a low profile of approximately 0.02λ at the lowest operating frequency. The measured results demonstrate an effective operating bandwidth of 5.16–5.68 GHz, corresponding to 9.6%, with isolation better than 19 dB and a peak gain of 9.4 dBi. In addition, the antenna exhibits good diversity performance in terms of envelope correlation coefficient (ECC), channel capacity loss (CCL), and mean effective gain (MEG). These results confirm that the proposed antenna is a promising candidate for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communication systems.
nfd3bd9bc416a: Background Sleep duration is increasingly recognized as a component of cardiovascular health, yet its prognostic significance among adults with established heart disease remains unclear. We examined associations between sleep duration and mortality among US adults with heart disease. Methods We analyzed data from 3,287 adults with heart disease participating in the 2004 National Health Interview Survey linked to the National Death Index through December 31, 2019. Sleep duration was categorized as ≤6 hours, 7–8 hours, and ≥9 hours. Cox proportional hazards models stratified by variables violating the proportional hazards assumption estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for all-cause, heart-related, and non-heart-related mortality. Restricted cubic splines evaluated nonlinear dose-response relationships. Results During 15 years of follow-up, 49.4% of participants died, including 16.7% from heart-related causes and 32.6% from non-heart-related causes. Compared with 7–8 hours of sleep, long sleep duration (≥9 hours) was associated with higher risks of all-cause mortality (HR:1.51 [95% CI:1.32–1.73]), heart-related mortality (HR:1.53 [95% CI:1.22–1.92]), and non-heart-related mortality (HR:1.50 [95% CI:1.27–1.77]). Restricted cubic spline analyses demonstrated nonlinear associations, with the lowest predicted mortality risk occurring at 6–7 hours. Findings remained robust across multiple sensitivity analyses and age and sex subgroups. Conclusions Among US adults with heart disease, long sleep duration was consistently associated with higher risks of all-cause, heart-related, and non-heart-related mortality. Sleep duration may represent a simple marker of residual risk that could enhance risk stratification among adults living with heart disease.
n800587a03b39: Located in the arid hinterland of Central Asia, the mountain temperate deserts in Xinjiang are jointly shaped by elevational geographic constraints and the east-west-oriented drought stress gradient. Nevertheless, the joint coupling relationships between these two gradient factors and community-level vegetation structural attributes across woody and herbaceous plant functional groups remain unclarified quantitatively at present. In this study, we investigated four community structural attributes (plant height, vegetation coverage, population density, and aboveground biomass) across four plant life forms, namely shrubs, semi-shrubs, perennial herbs, and annual herbs, along elevational, latitudinal, and longitudinal gradients in five major desert sub-regions of northern Xinjiang: Altay (n = 159), Tacheng–Yili (n = 164), Bortala and Changji–Urumqi(n = 110) and Eastern Tianshan (n = 94).In total, 527 sampling plots were surveyed during the plant growing season from May to mid-September(Desert field surveys conducted each year from May to September for a total of 3 years); plot numbers were unevenly distributed across subregions according to landscape accessibility and habitat representativeness. No temporal repeated measurements on identical permanent plots were conducted, and all analyses were based on one-off spatial snapshot observations from each plot. Trend-fitting, Single-gradient pattern analysis were applied to examine the correlational relationships between geographic gradients and community structural attributes. The results of this study are as follows: (1) Community structural attributes exhibited pronounced spatial heterogeneity and mostly showed unimodal or parabolic trends along the elevational gradient, with relatively high community performance concentrated in the mid-elevation range of 700–1100 m. This observed elevational unimodal pattern is consistent with the expectation of the mid-domain effect, yet such hump-shaped distributions can also arise from climatic, edaphic or topographic filtering and cannot serve as definitive direct empirical evidence for geometric mid-domain constraints. (2) Community-level vegetation performance tended to decline from the relatively humid western subregions (Tacheng-Yili-Bortala) toward the hyper-arid eastern subregions (Changji-Urumqi, Eastern Tianshan), corresponding to the west-to-east decreasing precipitation gradient driven by westerly circulation. (3) Different plant life-forms displayed distinct correlational adaptive patterns along these combined geographic gradients: shrubs and semi-shrubs maintained relatively stable community dominance under drought and low-temperature conditions; perennial herbs tended to occur in relatively mesic mid-elevation habitats; annual herbs showed high responsiveness to water-related environmental variation. (4) Among surveyed subregions, Eastern Tianshan presented the lowest observed community-attribute values, while the Tacheng-Yili subregion exhibited the highest and most stable community structural status. Collectively, our findings demonstrate correlational associations of elevational constraints and the west-east drought gradient with community structural variation in mountain temperate desert plant assemblages. These observational results provide observational reference for developing region-targeted conservation, grazing management and ecological restoration strategies for Xinjiang’s desert grassland ecosystems.
nd662f439da6b: Small carnivores are generally more adaptable to human-dominated landscapes compared with large carnivores, but have received comparatively limited attention. We evaluated the single-season multi-species occupancy and temporal overlap of five small carnivores in Bagmati-Ratu Complex (BRC) of Madhesh Province, Nepal using camera-trap surveys during January to February 2023. Camera-trap data were used to evaluate single-season multi-species occupancy using Markov Chain Monte Carlo simulations to understand the impacts of anthropogenic and environmental variables on community-level occupancy of small carnivores. We also calculated pairwise activity overlap coefficients (Dhat1) to examine temporal interactions among species. We observed the highest detection probability for jungle cat (Felis chaus; p = 0.315), whereas the lowest detection probability was for leopard cat (Prionailurus bengalensis; p = 0.245). Occupancy was highest for common palm civet (0.698), whereas lowest for large Indian civet (Viverra zibetha; 0.651). The community-level occupancy was negatively associated with area of farmland, whereas settlement area was positively associated at species-level only. All species exhibited strong nocturnal activity patterns, except the jungle cat, which showed some diurnal activity. We found high temporal overlap between the common palm civet and small Indian civet, consistent with their nocturnal behavior (Dhat1 = 0.77). All small carnivores exhibited similar activity patterns, with the reduced activity during the daytime and increased activity from dusk through dawn, indicating strongly nocturnal behavior and suggesting temporal avoidance of humans. These baseline data provide valuable information for understanding the coexistence of humans and small carnivores and can inform future conservation strategies.
ne3a8f35d4172: Background Although China has made major advances in maternal health, city-level epidemiological evidence on maternal mortality remains scarce. Using maternal surveillance data from Taiyuan (2016–2024), we assessed trends in the maternal mortality ratio (MMR), examined causes of death, and identified associated factors to inform region-specific strategies for reducing MMR. Methods We extracted and validated data on maternal deaths and live births from the Taiyuan Municipal Maternal and Child Health Annual Reports. MMR was calculated per 100,000 live births. Poisson regression was used to examine temporal trends, and chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests were used for between-group comparisons. Analyses were stratified by geographic region, cause of death, and place of death; the study period was divided into three phases (2016–2018, 2019–2021, 2022–2024) for subgroup analysis. Results Between 2016 and 2024, Taiyuan recorded 424,392 live births and 33 maternal deaths, yielding an overall MMR of 7.76 per 100,000 live births (95% CI 5.35 to 10.92). Urban MMR declined significantly (P < 0.0001), whereas rural MMR showed no significant temporal change (P = 0.313) and remained higher than urban levels (9.57 vs 7.58 per 100,000). Indirect obstetric causes accounted for 66.7% of maternal deaths, compared with 33.3% for direct causes, with no significant temporal trends in either category. Women aged 30–39 years accounted for 63.6% of maternal deaths, and 83.9% of deaths occurred in tertiary hospitals. Conclusion Taiyuan has maintained a low MMR through sustained investment in maternal healthcare; however, substantial urban-rural disparities remain. Indirect obstetric causes predominated among maternal deaths, suggesting a transition in the spectrum of maternal causes of death. Continued efforts to strengthen rural maternal health services and promote equitable, life-course-oriented maternal care are essential to further reduce preventable maternal deaths.
n4409d0efe2bc: Aims To describe trends in diabetic ketoacidosis admissions and examine factors associated with repeated admissions and mortality among adults living with type 1 diabetes. Materials and methods Diabetic ketoacidosis admissions among adults at a Norwegian university hospital between 1 August 2012 and 31 August 2022 were retrospectively reviewed using electronic medical records. Results A total of 178 participants with 306 admissions were included. Median [IQR] age at admission was 34 years [22–51]. Median HbA1c was 88 mmol/mol [72–105]. Diabetic ketoacidosis admission frequency decreased by an estimated 6.9% annually (RR 0.931; 95% CI 0.896–0.968; p < 0.001) over the 10-year period. 40 participants (22.5%) had more than one admission during the study period. Psychiatric illness (aOR 2.827; 95% CI 1.070–7.468; p = 0.036) and receipt of disability benefits (aOR 4.941; 95% CI 1.576–15.490; p = 0.006) were associated with experiencing more than one lifetime admission. Prior diabetic ketoacidosis, suspected treatment non-adherence and psychiatric illness were associated with higher readmission rates during follow-up. In-hospital mortality was 1.6%, and 5-year cumulative mortality was 14.7%. Alcohol or substance misuse (HR 2.499; 95% CI: 1.191–5.245; p = 0.015) and higher age at the index admission (HR 1.874; 95% CI: 1.511–2.324; p < 0.001, per 10 years) were associated with mortality in the follow-up period. Conclusions Diabetic ketoacidosis admissions declined substantially over the 10-year study period despite growth in the hospital catchment area population, suggesting that diabetes care has improved. Repeated admissions were common and associated with psychosocial vulnerability. In-hospital mortality was low, but five-year mortality was considerable, supporting targeted follow-up after an episode of diabetic ketoacidosis.
n12180a943ab6: The susceptibility of loess to water-induced deterioration poses a major threat to geotechnical stability. This study investigates the small-strain dynamic behavior of loess treated with tremella fuciformis polysaccharide (TFP), a sustainable biopolymer, using resonant column tests. The evolution of the maximum shear modulus (Gmax) and reference shear strain (γr) was systematically analyzed under varying applied confining pressures, water contents, and TFP dosages. Results show that for untreated loess, Gmax follows a power-law growth with confining pressure and linear attenuation with water content. TFP treatment significantly bolsters the small-strain shear stiffness; at a 2% dosage (σc = 150 kPa, w = 13%), Gmax increases from 63.12 MPa to 139.93 MPa. TFP treatment enhances the initial shear stiffness while altering the reference shear strain, indicating changes in the strain-dependent modulus reduction characteristics. A unified multi-factor model was developed to characterize the variations in Gmax and γr, providing a quantitative description of the strain-dependent modulus reduction behavior. SEM observations reveal film-like and filament-like features around soil particles, suggesting microstructural changes associated with TFP treatment. These findings highlight the potential of TFP as a sustainable bio-based approach to enhance the small-strain shear stiffness of loess, particularly under high-water-content conditions.
n261216b905b6: Routine athlete-monitoring data can test whether within-player changes in training load and wellness precede health problems, but sparse outcomes and incomplete reporting complicate inference. We conducted a reproducible secondary longitudinal analysis of the public SoccerMon dataset, comprising 50 players from two Norwegian elite women’s football teams monitored in 2020–2021. The outcome was onset on day t (the index player-day) of a self-reported lower-limb pain/injury episode after a 7-day episode washout. The primary risk set contained 42 onset-days from 15 players; the complete-case soreness interaction analysis contained 28 onset-days from nine event players. Under retrospective full-period within-player standardization, the focal acute-load x soreness interaction was estimated below 1.0 by Firth logistic regression (odds ratio [OR] 0.63, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.45–0.97), but uncertainty remained substantial. When within-player standardization was recalculated using only observations available before each day, the interaction attenuated to OR 0.97 (0.73–1.25). These data therefore do not provide stable evidence that within-player load deviations or load x wellness interactions are associated with next-day self-reported lower-limb pain onset. Sparse events, event concentration, missing monitoring data, and team/season imbalance further limit precision. In practice, daily load and wellness signals should be interpreted as contextual longitudinal information rather than as stand-alone next-day risk thresholds.
nc7292f28e0ef: A fundamental question of developmental biology is pattern formation, or how cells with specific gene expression end up in specific locations in the body to form tissues, organs, and, overall functional anatomy. Pattern formation involves communication through extracellular signals and complex intracellular gene networks integrating these signals to determine cell responses (e.g. further signaling, cell division, cell differentiation, etc.). In this article, we address two questions: (1) Are there any logical or mathematical principles determining which gene network topologies can lead to pattern formation by cell signaling over space in multicellular systems? (2) Can gene network topologies be classified into a small number of classes that entail similar dynamics and pattern transformation capacities? We combine logical arguments and mathematical proofs to show that, despite the large amount of formally possible gene network topologies, all gene network topologies capable of pattern formation fall into only three fundamental classes and their combinations. Additionally, we show that gene networks within each class share the same logic on how they lead to pattern formation, and hence, lead to similar patterns. We characterize the main features of each class. This zoo includes the complete gene networks that, to the best of our knowledge, have been experimentally reported to lead to pattern formation as well as other gene networks that have not yet been found experimentally.
nc3e6e7b599b0: Interest in the notion of animal agency is growing rapidly in different fields of academic inquiry. A wide range of disciplines are working to articulate an understanding of animals in fundamentally active terms, as creatures capable of shaping the way they engage with the world through exertion of choice, competence, and control. This review offers an integrated perspective on this development, outlining relevant discussions of animal agency in animal science as well as the social sciences and humanities, followed by an array of practical strategies for increasing the agency of animals in human care. The growing literature in these fields suggests that giving animals greater freedom to act and live as they prefer may in due course transform their role in science and society and substantially improve their well-being as a result.
n64d14ab77020: How 3D genome architecture varies across species, how it is encoded by molecular mechanisms and genomic sequence, and how it shapes animal evolution are questions that have become tractable only recently. Rapidly expanding chromatin-conformation data sets, chromosome-scale genome assemblies, and advances in computational modeling now enable comparative 3D genomics across broad phylogenetic scales. Here we review recent progress in 3D genome evolution, tracing how chromosome territories, polarized chromosome arrangements, compartments, and topologically associating domains have diversified across lineages. We examine the molecular and sequence determinants of this diversification, including condensin II, CCCTC-binding factor, alternative insulators, repetitive sequences, and large-scale chromosome rearrangements, and consider how architectural change may influence gene regulation, phenotypic divergence, and speciation. Finally, we discuss phylogeny-aware statistical models, sequence-to-contact map predictors, and emerging multimodal foundation models as complementary computational frameworks for identifying conserved and lineage-specific folding patterns, prioritizing sequence changes with predicted architectural effects, and generating testable evolutionary hypotheses.
n4f71aa9734a6: Epigenetic clocks have transformed aging research by providing accurate molecular measures of biological age, but the factors regulating their pace across mammals remain unclear. This review proposes a hierarchy of regulation: species-level determinants that set intrinsic aging rate and lifespan, as well as individual-level modifiers acting within species. Comparative analyses show developmental tempo, rather than body mass, anchors species differences. Across individuals, caloric restriction and other perturbations of the insulin-like growth factor 1 nutrient-sensing axis alter epigenetic aging rate, whereas torpor models suggest body temperature, rather than metabolic rate per se, acts as the pacemaker. Gonadal hormones, reproduction, social environment, and ecology also contribute, with applications in livestock and wildlife conservation highlighted as means to capitalize on age-associated traits and exposures. Together, this work shows epigenetic clocks are far more than a yardstick for biological time; they reveal the multifaceted biology, and its hierarchy, that sets the pace of aging in mammals.
n901aa81d4cd5: Sex-specific phenotypes arise from complex interactions among genetic, epigenetic, hormonal, and environmental factors throughout development and across the lifespan. Although sex-determination mechanisms establish gonadal identity, they also initiate differences in sex-specific responses beyond reproductive tissues. Here, we review the diverse genetic and environmental sex-determination systems, highlighting how these mechanisms regulate sex-specific gene expression. We further examine the roles of hormones, epigenetic modifications, and environmental factors in shaping physiological, behavioral, and life-history differences between the sexes. Early-life conditions, social environments, and reproductive strategies further modify these trajectories, producing substantial within- and among-species variations in sex-specific phenotypes during development and aging. By integrating evidence across vertebrates and invertebrates, we propose a unified framework in which sex-specific phenotypes emerge from dynamic interactions between genomes, epigenomes, and environments. This comparative perspective discusses conserved and lineage-specific principles underlying the evolution, phenotypic plasticity, and adaptive significance of sex differences across diverse taxa.
n0a4f42f29262: Safety limits on exposure to hazardous chemicals are typically treated as uniform across populations, but substantial variability exists between individuals. This review argues that susceptibility to chemical exposure should be understood as a complex genetic trait shaped by polygenic architecture, environmental context, and biological modifiers such as sex. Drawing on evidence from animal models, human-relevant test systems, and comparative genomics, we show that variation in toxic response is structured, heritable, and frequently predictable. We critically evaluate the limitations of traditional toxicology, which relies on simplified models and average responses, and highlight how this deterministic approach fails to capture population-level risk. We further examine genotype × sex interactions and the contribution of rare variants to extreme sensitivity. Finally, we discuss emerging risk assessment frameworks, including population-based and probabilistic approaches, and consider their implications for regulatory decision-making. Recognizing toxicological susceptibility as a complex trait provides a more realistic and protective basis for chemical risk assessment.
ned43a21e82b7: The prevalence of chronic kidney disease (CKD) in aging felids is three- to four-fold higher than in other mammals, including humans. Regardless of species, serum and urinary biomarkers of CKD become effective only when little can be done to reverse progression. We propose that felids, as super water conservers and obligate hyper-carnivores, are naturally prone to form cytoplasmic lipid droplets (LDs) in their kidney cells, which predisposes felids to age-associated CKD. Furthermore, we offer a novel mechanistic basis for renal LD formation in felids. Presence of LDs in felid urine—lipuria, which is uncommon in all other mammals—could be the earliest biomarker of metabolic events in kidney cells that underpin CKD. Felids have unique anatomical, physiological, nutritional, and metabolic features, including synthesis and subsequent excretion of felinine together with branched-chain fatty acids into urine. These features offer a unique opportunity for early intervention but also are of interest in the context of comparative biology, nephrology, and renal disease.
n439d3450da5d: Adult stem cell aging and malignant transformation are inextricably linked through a complex interplay of intrinsic cellular dysfunction and extrinsic microenvironmental remodeling. Together, these factors generate a positive feedback loop that drives quiescent, tightly regulated stem cells toward dysregulated, mutation-enriched states characterized by a loss of lineage fidelity. This review synthesizes literature detailing how age-associated alterations, including epigenetic drift, genomic instability, telomere dynamics, and metabolic rewiring, converge with extracellular matrix remodeling, paracrine shifts, and inflammaging to foster permissive tissue niches. Furthermore, we discuss the mechanisms and consequences of somatic mosaicism, notably clonal hematopoiesis, in relation to malignant risk. Finally, we highlight current and potential clinical interception strategies designed to mitigate clonal expansion, optimize risk assessment, and disrupt oncogenesis across diverse human tissues.
nd4522b6edb6c: Quantitative modeling has become an essential tool in modern biology, driven by advances in both experimental techniques and theoretical frameworks. Powerful high-resolution techniques now provide detailed datasets spanning molecular to tissue scales, allowing visualization of cellular structures with unprecedented detail. In parallel, developments in soft and active matter physics have established a robust theoretical basis for describing biological systems. In this context, two main modeling paradigms have emerged: particle-based models, which explicitly represent discrete components and their interactions, and continuum models, which describe systems through spatially varying fields. We compare these approaches across biological scales, highlighting their respective strengths, limitations, and domains of applicability. To keep our discussion biologically relevant, we focus on five systems of fundamental importance: the cytoskeleton, membranes, chromatin, biomolecular condensates and tissues. With this review, we aim to provide a framework for both theorists and experimentalists to select appropriate modeling strategies, and highlight future directions in biophysical modeling.
ndf2e6e376e7e: We are taught that liquids flow while solids don’t. But as liquids are supercooled below their freezing temperatures, their dynamics become increasingly slow until their flow becomes undetectable on reasonable timescales—this is the glass transition. Conversely, when glasses are put under mechanical load, they can flow very sluggishly—this is plasticity. In both of these glass problems, flow involves microscopic hops, in which constituent particles change their neighbors. For decades, no link between local structure and hops was found for either of these two glass problems, but it is easily detected using machine learning. We review a machine-learned local structural quantity, softness, which is predictive of hops, describing what it teaches us about both glass problems.
n51b8f09574c2: 3D scene graphs (3DSGs) have emerged as a powerful representation for spatial AI by combining geometric grounding with semantic and relational abstractions of the environment. Their expressiveness has made them relevant to a broad range of problems in robotics and computer vision, including manipulation, navigation, task planning, scene understanding, and many others. However, the field remains fragmented: Different communities adopt distinct formulations, construction pipelines, and evaluation protocols, making it difficult to compare methods, identify common assumptions, and assess remaining challenges for robust real-world deployment. This survey provides a unified and critical review of 3DSGs, with particular emphasis on open challenges and future directions. We first formalize 3DSGs under a common definition and analyze the principal modeling choices that characterize existing formulations, including node and edge attributes, hierarchical structure, dynamic scene representations, and affordance-aware extensions. We then review how 3DSGs are built from raw sensory observations, discussing the most common terminologies, conventions, and techniques. Finally, we examine downstream applications and evaluation strategies, from intrinsic graph quality to task-level performance. To support the community, we also provide a dedicated website that organizes and extends the surveyed content, accessible at https://3dscenegraphs.com .
n8d5bec1aece3: ▪ Wildfire events are increasing in intensity and frequency around the globe, and the resulting smoke degrades air quality. Following emission, particulate matter and reactive gases in smoke chemically transform during transport through the near- (hours), mid- (days), and far-field (weeks). The chemical composition of the smoke, its intensity, and subsequent human exposure will vary as a function of not only the properties of the original wildfire but also the subsequent atmospheric chemistry. This chemistry impacts particles, ozone, volatile organic compounds, and other air toxics in urban and rural regions, and thus affects human and ecosystem health. This review synthesizes recent work and identifies key knowledge gaps in the atmospheric chemistry of the smoke plume, smoke composition from fires at the wildland-urban interface, smoke-building interactions and remediation approaches to improve indoor air, and biosphere-atmosphere exchange, including effects on plant productivity and gas exchange. Wildfire smoke is chemically complex with gases and particles that dilute, react, and transform over timescales ranging from minutes to weeks. ▪ Wildfire smoke enhances production of ozone and particulate matter in cities, increasing urban air pollution. ▪ Smoke infiltrates buildings, exposing occupants to pollutants during and after the smoke event, highlighting research needs on wildland-urban interface fires. ▪ Ecosystem productivity can increase or decrease in response to smoke depending on the intensity and location, raising concerns about future crop yield and quality.
n8b09b724e50c: Here I recount with pleasure the twists and turns in my academic career and reflect on the many serendipitous events that have shaped the trajectory of my life. Beginning with my twin loves, molecular biology and animal behavior, I describe how I navigated between these disparate passions. Extreme fondness for the organisms and concepts I studied, a relentless desire to live and work in India with all its rewards and limitations, and a determination to do cutting-edge research without recourse to large grants and sophisticated laboratories have been the principal drivers of my scientific life. Understanding everything humanly possible about the society of Indian paper wasps, Ropalidia marginata , became my life's goal although I got there from unexpected and convoluted beginnings.
nc80b515775ea: Agrilus mali Matsumura, native to northeast Asia, is now widespread in western China and Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region and is knocking on the door of central Asia, the Garden of Eden for the ancestor of domestic apples. The interpretation of invasions poses many challenges: Where did the species originate, how did it arrive, what are the host plants at risk, and was it always present but very rare? We review the evidence for range expansion in A. mali and how it most likely spread. We highlight what has been learned since the invasion and devastation in outbreak areas but are critical of what has not been done well and needs to be done better to put mitigation measures on a firm foundation. An integrated approach to infestations centered on timely pruning of A. mali –infested branches is highly effective for management. On balance, the evidence suggests A. mali is destined to be yet another invasive buprestid.
n3c48dc905a46: Since the discovery of insulin in 1921, there has been remarkable evolution in insulin treatment for diabetes, with modern insulin analogues utilizing highly engineered recombinant technology. The purpose of this review is to focus on two revolutionary developments in contemporary insulin therapy: once-weekly ultralong-acting basal insulins and ultrashort-acting bolus insulins. Insulin icodec and insulin efsitora alfa represent a unique shift in basal insulin delivery, offering the convenience of once-weekly administration, flat pharmacokinetic profiles, and glycemic efficacy and safety comparable to those of daily basal analogues while reducing injection burden and improving patient satisfaction. With regard to bolus therapy, faster-acting aspart and ultrarapid lispro achieve accelerated absorption through novel excipient engineering, enabling more flexible mealtime dosing and improved postprandial glucose control compared to their traditional counterparts. Looking ahead, there are promising innovations on the horizon, including glucose-responsive insulins, artificial intelligence–driven automated insulin delivery, and the continued pursuit of oral insulin. Together, these advances represent an accelerating trajectory toward more physiological, convenient, and, most importantly, safe insulin therapy.
ndfd82a6d6451: The interior of living cells is highly crowded with proteins, nucleic acids, and metabolites—a setting that simultaneously demands large system sizes and long simulation timescales. Exascale computing, now realized on modern supercomputers, offers a qualitatively new opportunity to address this challenge. In this review, we examine how multiscale molecular dynamics simulations—spanning all-atom, coarse-grained, and ultra-coarse-grained representations—are transforming our understanding of macromolecular crowding and liquid–liquid phase separation. We survey recent advances in force-field development, machine-learning-assisted system construction, and high-performance computing–optimized molecular dynamics engines, with particular attention to how these tools make large-scale simulations practically feasible. Key physical insights discussed include the interplay between excluded volume and nonspecific sticky interactions, crowding-induced slowdown of diffusion, metabolite-binding kinetics, and the regulatory mechanisms governing biomolecular condensate formation and maturation. We outline how exascale platforms, integrated with machine learning and experimental data, are bringing predictive whole-cell simulations within reach.
ne78cba0877c6: Brain precapillary sphincters (PSs) are located at the point where the penetrating arteriole meets the first-order capillary. Sphincters link blood flow in the capillaries to arteriolar inflow. The sphincters are encircled by contractile mural cells that can control the length and width of the enclosed vessel segment in both directions. Hemodynamic consequences include the ability of PSs to generate the largest changes in cerebrovascular flow resistance of all brain vessel segments. Using two-photon microscopy and genetically encoded reporters, we have revealed the physiology of sphincters. Our work has shown that sphincters can increase their diameter by approximately 30% within a few seconds, enabling rapid control of capillary blood flow over a wide dynamic range. In this article, we discuss the morphology and functions of sphincters, outlining their central role in rapidly adjusting blood flow in the microcirculation and protecting brain tissue against blood pressure variations in the cardiac cycle.
na8245e2152b9: A growing body of evidence demonstrates that commercial entities play an important role in shaping the prevalence, incidence, and distribution of obesity. This narrative review examines policy solutions to address the commercial determinants of obesity. We describe how five business sectors (food, beverages, and agriculture; media and entertainment; sports and recreation; transportation; and medical care and pharmaceuticals) shape obesity prevalence through three key behavioral pathways: diet, physical activity, and use of medical care. We then examine four categories of tools available to national and subnational governments to address the commercial determinants: legal and regulatory measures, fiscal policies, market governance mechanisms, and litigation. Finally, we discuss three strategies that can support the successful implementation of these measures: building cross-sectoral support, limiting undue influence in policymaking processes, and designing policies informed by precedent and designed to withstand challenges. We conclude by highlighting key insights for policymakers seeking to make measurable progress in preventing and reducing obesity.
n5ff3ff0bc22a: Fairness is context dependent and multifaceted. Many jurisdictions prohibit insurers from discriminating on sensitive characteristics, such as race or gender, in insurance pricing. However, some direct or indirect discrimination is inevitable: Allowed rating factors and protected characteristics are associated. As solidarity (risk pooling) and actuarial fairness (premiums proportional to expected losses) have always formed the core tension in insurance pricing, causality has recently emerged as a third essential fairness dimension. We present the dominant unfairness mitigation approaches: autocalibration, which reduces cross-subsidies; discrimination-free insurance pricing and its extensions, which mitigate proxy effects; and optimal transport approaches, which eliminate disparities. We situate the methods within a broader taxonomy of fairness methodologies. We discuss some statistical challenges to implementing antidiscrimination regulation, including the choice of sensitive characteristics, measurement under data privacy, diagnosis of unfairness in finite sample, and generalization beyond an insurer's portfolio.
nd3b17a4b8a59: Multimodal analysis in neuroscience has become increasingly important as brain research comes to rely more heavily on integrated analysis of multiple neuroimaging modalities and complementary data sources. In this review, we adopt a statistics-centered perspective, organizing the literature around three core scientific questions: cross-modal association, which focuses on characterizing shared structure and dependence across modalities; outcome association and prediction, which examine how multimodal signals contribute to clinical and behavioral outcomes; and brain causal analysis, which seeks to identify directed effects and mechanistic pathways. We then discuss some emerging trends, especially the integration of unstructured, nontabular data such as clinical and radiology reports, and the growing heterogeneity of data collected across multiple cohorts, sites, and acquisition protocols. Our central message is that multimodal neuroimaging analysis goes beyond simple data fusion and requires a principled statistical foundation, one that enables clear problem formulation, provides valid and efficient inference, and ensures robustness, as modern neuroimaging and complementary data become more complex and heterogeneous.
ned9c86ad0855: Astrostatistics lies at the interface of astrophysics and statistics and has been growing for over two decades. Reasons for this growth include big datasets in astronomy that are often publicly available, the use of physically motivated mathematical models in inference, and the need for innovative and efficient statistical and computational methods. To highlight the kinds of statistical challenges and opportunities available in astrostatistics, we focus in this review on a specific type of astronomical objects called globular clusters. These star clusters are some of the oldest objects in the universe and are deceptively simple in appearance. In the context of studying them, we introduce and highlight challenges and opportunities related to modeling, data, inference, and computation that should be of interest to statisticians. We hope this review will inspire statisticians to become involved not only in the study of globular clusters but also in astrostatistics.
n8df597e91947: The vast collection of human-specific traits—such as our unique morphology, cognition, behavior, and diseases—has long been attributed to gene expression divergence between us and our closest living relatives, chimpanzees. Theory suggests that changes to cis-regulatory elements such as promoters and enhancers may drive evolutionary adaptation, and DNA methylation is a key factor in transcriptional cis-regulation. However, we still lack an understanding of (1) how species-specific methylation patterns arise; (2) their downstream effects; and (3) whether they are a common target of natural selection. In this study, we investigated these three questions. By combining a novel hypothesis testing framework with DNA methylation data from six human and chimpanzee cell types, as well as fused interspecies hybrid cells, we disentangled cis- vs. trans-acting methylation divergence across the genome. Across cell types, we found that methylation divergence is primarily driven in cis, which can be linked in some cases to nearby sequence variants such as CpG gains and losses. Although less common, regions with trans-acting methylation divergence were enriched for specific transcription factor (TF) binding motifs, suggesting a role of TFs such as FOXM1 in these differences. Having established these causes of methylation divergence, we then examined the functional consequences of differential methylation. Although methylation lacks a consistent relationship with transcription, we observed that associations between methylation and gene expression are stronger for genes with cis-regulatory divergence. Moreover, we identified lineage-specific selection shaping promoter methylation at the level of entire pathways, including those associated with human-specific traits such as speech, cognition, and susceptibility to infection with hepatitis C. Collectively, our findings provide a mechanistic framework suggesting that DNA methylation may occupy a key position, mediating the effects of both cis- and trans-acting factors on transcriptional networks, including those contributing to human-specific traits.
nfa70cafd3cc8: The ability to update the valence of sensory perception to influence behavior is crucial for survival. A common phenotype in autism spectrum disorders (ASDs) is defects in sensory processing, but whether these defects impair flexible sensory encoding is largely unexplored. In particular, how genetic risk factors such as Shank3 deletion affect the adaptability of cortical taste processing and downstream behavior is unknown. To address this gap, we performed two-photon calcium imaging during a conditioned taste aversion (CTA) learning paradigm, an ethologically relevant form of associative learning that depends on taste processing in the gustatory cortex (GC), to examine how Shank3 knockout alters taste-related neuronal activity in GC and influences CTA learning. We found that GC neurons in Shank3 knockout mice exhibited reduced stimulus-evoked suppression and increased trial-to-trial correlated variability during the acquisition of CTA memory. These activity changes, which likely reduced signal-to-noise ratio in GC, were associated with slower CTA acquisition in Shank3 knockout mice. In both genotypes, CTA learning enhanced, while subsequent extinction reduced, taste discriminability in GC, and both extinction and the associated reduction in discriminability were faster in Shank3 knockout than in wild-type mice. Together, these results show that Shank3 loss is associated with destabilized cortical activity dynamics in GC, which may contribute to inefficient encoding and maintenance of learned taste aversion. These findings show that loss of Shank3 compromises the ability of animals to update behavior to incorporate negative outcomes, and suggest this loss of flexibility may be an important feature of monogenic ASDs.
n1a23df089a7a: During times of environmental stress, many animals enter torpor: a reversible protective physiological state typically characterised by reductions in core temperature, heart rate, and oxygen consumption. Species that naturally enter this hypothermic and hypometabolic state are tolerant of ischaemia-reperfusion injury. Consequently, there is a growing interest in utilising aspects of torpor for clinical applications such as protection from stroke or myocardial infarction. It is currently unknown, however, whether a torpor-like state is protective in animals that do not naturally enter torpor. Using viral vector-mediated chemogenetic activation of the medial preoptic area of the hypothalamus, we induced synthetic torpor in the rat, a species that does not naturally enter torpor. We demonstrate this state is cardioprotective in an ex vivo ischaemia-reperfusion injury model with an ~40% reduction in infarct size. Synthetic torpor-induced cardioprotection of the normothermic, isolated heart is not dependent on prior hypothermia in vivo. Phosphoproteomic analysis of cardiac tissue indicates that the protective effects of synthetic torpor may be mediated by parallel activation of cell survival and stress tolerance pathways and inhibition of cell death pathways. These findings provide important insights into the mechanisms of organ protective effects of synthetic torpor states with implications for future clinical translation in humans.
ne01686a1bac4: Most patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) are diagnosed with coronary heart disease (CHD). The triglyceride glucose‑body mass index (TyG‑BMI) has been reported to be associated with CHD. This study aimed to investigate the association between TyG‑BMI and the risk of repeat PCI among post‑PCI patients, with additional exploratory stratification analyses according to glucose‑metabolism status. Data for this study were derived from resident health‑record follow‑up records of Yipeng Community Health Service Center, covering January 2015 to January 2025. Logistic regression models and restricted cubic spline (RCS) were used to evaluate the association between TyG‑BMI and the risk of repeat PCI among post‑PCI patients, with exploratory stratification by glucose‑metabolism status. Logistic regression and restricted cubic spline analyses showed no significant linear or nonlinear association between TyG‑BMI and repeat PCI (OR=0.999,95%CI:0.994 ~ 1.003, P = 0.534; nonlinear χ2 = 0.91, df = 3, P = 0.8223). Stratified analyses by glucose metabolism status also revealed no significant correlation in any stratum(P > 0.05). No independent association between TyG‑BMI and repeat PCI was identified in post‑PCI patients, even within different glucose‑metabolism strata. Relevant findings require further verification in larger prospective cohorts.
neb3507a8ef09: Colchicine has been associated with reduced cardiovascular events in secondary prevention, but evidence for primary prevention is limited. We examined the association between colchicine use and cardiovascular outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and gout without prior coronary artery disease. From the Korean National Health Insurance Service database, we identified 48,295 patients with diabetes and gout without prior coronary artery disease between 2015 and 2019. We compared 28,964 colchicine users with 19,331 non-users by 1:1 propensity score matching, which produced 17,337 matched pairs. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, and nonfatal stroke. The primary composite outcome occurred in 12.52% of colchicine users versus 15.03% of non-users (hazard ratio [HR] 0.71; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.66–0.75; P < 0.001). All-cause mortality was significantly reduced in colchicine users (8.01% vs. 11.07%; HR 0.58; 95% CI 0.53–0.62; P < 0.001). No significant differences were observed for myocardial infarction (HR 1.15; 95% CI 0.96–1.37; P = 0.121) or stroke (HR 0.91; 95% CI 0.81–1.01; P = 0.076). In a landmark analysis at 365 days that addressed immortal time bias, the associations with all-cause mortality (HR 0.67; 95% CI 0.62–0.73; P < 0.001) and with the composite outcome (HR 0.76; 95% CI 0.71–0.81; P < 0.001) remained significant, whereas stroke (HR 0.99; 95% CI 0.87–1.12; P = 0.823) and myocardial infarction (HR 1.15; 95% CI 0.95–1.40; P = 0.144) did not differ between the two groups. In patients with diabetes and gout without prior coronary artery disease, colchicine use was associated with lower all-cause mortality. The reduction in the composite outcome was driven by mortality rather than by myocardial infarction or stroke.
n366a12ec0a4a: Inactivated influenza vaccines (IIVs) often fail to provide robust mucosal protection, necessitating the development of potent adjuvants for intranasal delivery. This study evaluated a novel adjuvant combination of Monophosphoryl lipid A (MPL), a TLR4 agonist, and alpha-Galactosyl Ceramide (α-GalCer), an NKT cell ligand, to enhance the efficacy of an intranasal inactivated A/PR8 (iPR8) influenza vaccine. In vitro results demonstrated that MPL+ α-GalCer increased the frequencies of CD4⁺ CD25⁺ , CD8⁺ CD25⁺ and CD4⁺ CD69⁺ T cells relative to both the vehicle control and either single adjuvant in splenocyte cultures, whereas in purified dendritic cell and macrophage cultures MPL+ α-GalCer was no more effective than MPL alone. Splenocyte supernatants showed higher elevated TNF- α, IL-2, IFN-γ, IL-4, and IL-13. This pre-activation drove robust allogeneic T-cell proliferation in a mixed lymphocyte reaction, indicating enhanced allostimulatory capacity rather than influenza-specific priming. In vivo, a single intranasal dose of iPR8+ MPL+ α-GalCer elicited high systemic IgG titers and was effective at inducing Th1-associated IgG2a alongside IgG1. Following an LD50-range PR8 challenge, the combined-adjuvant group showed 100% survival, which was not statistically significant and lower lung viral titers at 7 days post-infection. This group exhibited elevated post-challenge lung-associated antigen-specific IgA and a reduced viral burden, which was accompanied by lower inflammatory cell infiltration and cytokine levels. The protection of combination group was accompanied by increased frequencies of ex vivo antigen-responsive CD4+ and CD8+ T cells recovered post-challenge. Our findings suggest that the MPL+ α-GalCer combination enhances innate and adaptive immune responses, providing an effective adjuvant platform for homologous mucosal protection in a murine model.
n24bd189ddb32: Emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants continue to demand orally tractable, non-covalent inhibitors of the conserved main protease (Mpro). Here, chromone-phenyl-tetrazole hybrids were prioritized using a multiscale computational strategy that connects drug-likeness, binding stability, free-energy ranking, conformational behavior, and quantum-level electronic features. The series showed favorable oral drug-like profiles and low-to-moderate predicted acute toxicity. Among the stable Mpro complexes, M2 displayed the strongest computed affinity (MM/GBSA ΔGbind = −38.8 kcal·mol ⁻ ¹), driven mainly by dispersion with limited desolvation cost, whereas M4 showed the most direct catalytic-dyad engagement through His41/Cys145-supported anchoring. DFT analysis rationalized these complementary profiles: M2 and M4 exhibited narrower HOMO-LUMO gaps (4.00 eV) and higher electronic softness, while ELF/NCI maps revealed heteroatom-centered electron reservoirs and weak intramolecular preorganization. The derived pharmacophore consists of a planar chromone π-platform bearing a carbonyl/phenolic acceptor-donor edge, a para-phenyl spacer for conjugation and hydrophobic occupancy, and a methoxy-tetrazole polar/π-rich head for Glu166/Phe140/His163 anchoring. Overall, M2 and M4 emerge as complementary lead chemotypes for experimental validation and structure-guided optimization against Mpro.
n3673d0153d0c: This paper examines a supply chain comprising a single new energy vehicle manufacturer (NEVM) and a single power battery supplier (PBS), considering government subsidies and R&D outcome uncertainty. An exponential function is employed to characterize R&D outcome uncertainty. The impacts of R&D subsidies and R&D capability on R&D investment, supply chain members, and their expected profits are examined. A comparative analysis of cost-sharing (CS) and revenue-sharing (RS) contracts is conducted. The findings reveal that: (1) R&D investment exhibits an inverted U-shaped relationship with R&D capability and a positive relationship with R&D subsidies. (2) Under an RS contract, the expected profits of the supply chain and its members increase with higher R&D subsidies and enhanced R&D capability. Under a CS contract, the expected profits of the PBS and the supply chain increase with higher R&D subsidies and enhanced R&D capability; however, the NEVM’s expected profit exhibits a U-shaped relationship with R&D subsidies and R&D capability. (3) Compared with centralized decision-making, neither contract achieves the centralized benchmark for the supply chain’s expected profit. However, compared with decentralized decision-making, the CS contract increases the PBS’s R&D investment and expected profit; the RS contract increases the PBS’s R&D investment and expected profit as well as the supply chain’s expected profit. Both contracts can only improve the NEVM’s expected profit under certain conditions. These findings provide valuable theoretical insights and practical implications for decision-making by NEVMs, PBSs, and government agencies.
