n91ec2448c1f6: To address the structural complexity and limited compliance of traditional rigid robotic wrists, as well as the absence of adjustable stiffness in soft wrists designed primarily for flexibility, a two-degree-of-freedom (2-DOF) pneumatic flexible wrist with controllable braking torque was developed. The wrist comprises three circumferentially arranged pneumatic actuators connected in parallel around a central pneumatic cross-hinge brake, enabling multidirectional pivoting, while the braking torque can be adjusted according to task requirements for pose stabilization. This configuration combines the high stiffness required for posture maintenance during braking with compliant actuation during motion. Theoretical models of the wrist pivot angle, pivoting direction, and braking torque were established. The pivot-angle model was empirically calibrated using the measured pivot-angle data, while the pivoting-direction and braking-torque models were validated experimentally. Mechanical performance was evaluated under constant-friction-torque and constant-pivot-angle conditions, and empirical relations were obtained by fitting the experimental data. A three-dimensional motion-capture system was also used to characterize the dynamic response under different braking conditions and excitation signals. Under the present experimental conditions, the results show that the wrist exhibits high compliance and enables continuous omnidirectional pivoting with a maximum single-axis pivot angle of 45.2°. The pneumatic cross‑hinge brake achieves multidirectional braking with continuously adjustable torque, reaching a maximum braking torque of 0.842 N·m under brake-only actuation at 0.35 MPa. During coordinated actuation–braking operation, the wrist’s overall resistance to external loads increased by a factor of 4.98 compared with its unpressurized initial state. This composite load-resisting capacity originates from the combined effects of the pneumatic actuators and the central brake.
n0b2f4f08d805: To ensure standardization, reliability, and maximal performance, physical performance tests are usually performed with little to no cognitive load. However, during training and competition, athletes usually perform physical actions while under the demands of a concurrent cognitive task (CT). This study examined the effect of a concurrent CT on the force-time metrics of the drop jump (DJ) and their reliability under single-task (DJ without a CT) and dual-task conditions (DJ with a CT based on simple arithmetic calculations). Thirty-five healthy young participants performed single-task and dual-task DJ trials in a randomized order. Nineteen force-time metrics covering the braking, propulsion, and landing phases of the DJ were compared between conditions using paired t-tests with Holm adjustment and Hedges’ gz, Bayesian paired t-tests, and statistical parametric mapping (SPM) of vertical ground reaction force (VGRF) waveforms. For three-trial mean scores, 17 of the 19 metrics had within-session intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) of 0.812–0.930 across both conditions. Under the dual-task condition, jump height (p < 0.001, gz=1.40, Bayes factor BF10 = 1.76×107) and reactive strength index (p < 0.001, gz=1.04, BF10 = 45,943) were lower, while ground contact time was longer (p = 0.025, gz=−0.57, BF10 = 20.57). SPM showed that VGRF was significantly lower under the dual-task condition during 29.2–34.3% (within braking) and 52.0–79.1% (within propulsion) of ground contact. In the landing phase, VGRF was significantly lower under the dual-task condition during 1.3–6.3% (initial force rise) and significantly higher during 15.5–19.6% (attenuation of the impact force). The spring-like correlation (p = 0.462, gz=0.20, BF01 = 2.79) and the vertical time to stabilization (p = 0.462, gz=0.15, BF01 = 3.74) showed no significant difference between conditions, with weak and moderate evidence for the absence of an effect. These findings suggest that a concurrent CT reduces force production within both the braking and propulsion phases of the DJ and alters the VGRF waveform during the subsequent landing phase in healthy young participants.
n82d622dc493e: Background UHRF1 has been established as a susceptibility gene in multiple cancer types; however, its functional role in the pathogenesis of adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATLL) remains poorly defined. This study aimed to investigate UHRF1 expression in ATLL and assess its clinical and biological significance. Methods Immunohistochemistry was performed to evaluate UHRF1 protein expression in tumor tissues from 72 ATLL patients and 30 reactive lymphadenopathy controls. Univariate Cox’s proportional hazard regression model was used to screen the factors affecting OS and PFS, and multivariate Cox’s proportional hazard regression model was used to screen independent prognostic factors in ATLL. UHRF1 expression in the HuT-102 ATLL cell line and MT-4 cell line was evaluated by Western blotting and quantitative PCR, and shRNA-mediated knockdown was used to assess proliferation and apoptosis. Results UHRF1 protein was highly expressed in primary ATLL samples (P < 0.001, median 26.562 vs. 1.306), and the percentage of positive pixels (%Area) significantly higher than that in the control group (P < 0.001, median 9.914 vs. 0.574). Multivariate Cox regression analysis demonstrated that UHRF1 expression remained an independent prognostic predictor after adjustment for clinicopathological characteristics. For overall survival (OS): P = 0.026, HR = 2.397, 95%CI: 1.108–5.184; for progression-free survival (PFS): P = 0.042, HR = 1.959, 95%CI: 1.025–3.744. Mechanistically, UHRF1 knockdown significantly suppressed proliferation and induced apoptosis in ATLL cell lines (HuT-102 cells and MT-4 cell). Co-immunoprecipitation detected no stable interaction between UHRF1 and either AMPK or the PP2A catalytic subunit PPP2CA, and UHRF1 knockdown did not significantly alter LKB1, PPP2R4, or the p-AMPK (Thr172)/AMPK ratio; whether UHRF1 intersects with AMPK signaling remains to be determined. These findings identify UHRF1 as an independent adverse prognostic indicator in ATLL and provide preliminary biological evidence, though the underlying mechanisms require further validation in larger cohorts and in vivo models.
nf6e391fa075a: Family emotional processes play a central role in adolescent well-being, yet most research relies on dyadic or static approaches that do not capture the dynamic, system-level nature of family emotional life. In a sample of adolescents (ages 12–17), mothers, and fathers (N = 120; 2,365 assessments), constituting 40 family triads, we used ecological momentary assessment and a dynamic network approach to estimate how emotions fluctuate over time and co-vary across family members within each system. Emotional synchrony—defined as the extent to which family members’ affective states change together—was modeled at both overall (between-family) and momentary (within-family) levels. Results indicated that families exhibited greater synchrony in positive affect than negative affect, alongside substantial heterogeneity in network structures. At the person level, greater positive affect synchrony was associated with higher adolescent well-being and lower distress, whereas negative affect synchrony showed inverse patterns. At the momentary level, increases in negative affect synchrony were associated with higher concurrent well-being and lower stress. Many of these person-level associations were substantially attenuated once adolescents’ general affect levels were accounted for, whereas synchrony at the between-family level continued to predict adolescents’ momentary well-being beyond their concurrent affect. These findings highlight emotional synchrony as a dynamic property of family systems and underscore the importance of modeling family processes across multiple timescales.
n9f811f78e9d2: Classification of hospitalization outcomes in wildlife hospitals may support clinical assessment and resource planning, but model performance can vary across institutions with different case profiles and care practices. This study evaluated a previously developed random forest model for classifying hospitalization outcomes in Asian elephants using temporally distinct 2025 data from three elephant hospitals in Thailand. The validation comprised temporal validation at the original development center and institutional validation at two additional hospitals. Because length of stay was included as a predictor, the model was evaluated as a hospitalization-course classification model rather than as an admission-time prognostic tool. The final validation cohort comprised 237 hospitalization episodes contributed by 215 elephants, including 17 deceased, 36 ongoing, and 184 recovered episodes. Overall accuracy was 0.793, compared with 0.776 for a recovered-only majority-class classifier. Macro-averaged balanced accuracy was 0.732, the prevalence-weighted one-vs-rest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.854, and multiclass log loss was 0.617. Classification performance was stronger for ongoing and recovered episodes than for deceased episodes. The limited number of deceased episodes resulted in substantial uncertainty around mortality-focused performance and calibration estimates. Calibration patterns differed across outcome classes, with an overall multiclass Brier score of 0.323. In the binary deceased-versus-recovered sensitivity analysis, the AUC was 0.726 (95% confidence interval, 0.585–0.839), indicating moderate but imprecise discrimination. Overall, the model retained discriminatory information across the validation cohort, but its modest improvement over the majority-class benchmark, weaker deceased-class performance, and reliance on hospitalization-duration information warrant cautious interpretation. Further prospective evaluation is needed before routine clinical application.
nda9e722de8ef: In flotation-based mineral processing, froth images contain important visual information that reflects the operating condition of the process and provides a basis for process monitoring and control. However, conventional machine-vision methods still encounter difficulties in extracting static froth features under conditions of bubble adhesion, overlap, weak boundaries, and uneven illumination. To address these problems, a flotation froth image analysis framework is proposed by combining a boundary-aware U-Net segmentation model with a segmentation-guided adaptive Hough transform. In the first stage, the U-Net architecture is enhanced with explicit boundary-oriented supervision to improve the separation of adherent and overlapping bubbles. In the second stage, the geometric priors derived from the segmentation results are used to constrain the Hough-based detection process, thereby improving the reliability of bubble counting and geometric feature extraction. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves a Dice similarity coefficient of 96.39% and an intersection over union of 93.04%, while maintaining favorable inference efficiency. Compared with representative segmentation models, the proposed framework provides a better balance between accuracy and speed. The study demonstrates that the integration of deep boundary-aware segmentation and adaptive geometric detection is effective for static feature extraction of flotation froth images and has potential for intelligent monitoring of flotation processes.
ne4c46b9af53f: Background Antibiotic-sparing strategies, such as delayed prescribing or symptomatic therapy, can reduce antibiotic use in uncomplicated urinary tract infections (UTIs), yet their implementation in primary care remains inconsistent. Within this context, non-physician medical staff within general practices and community pharmacies play increasingly important roles in patient counselling and care coordination, potentially shaping treatment expectations and treatment decisions. This study investigated how general practitioners (GPs) make treatment decisions in the management of uncomplicated UTIs in women and examined their views on the roles of non-physician medical staff and community pharmacies in supporting antibiotic-sparing management. Methods We conducted an exploratory qualitative interview study with GPs who regularly manage women with uncomplicated UTIs. Virtual, semi-structured interviews were conducted. Interviews were transcribed verbatim and analyzed thematically. Results Fifteen GPs participated; their mean age was 46.6 years, 53.3% were female, and their experience in general practice ranged from 5 to 25 years. The thematic analysis generated six themes capturing clinical, relational, practical, and interprofessional influences on UTI management. Most GPs reported prior experience with antibiotic-sparing strategies, but thresholds for antibiotic prescribing varied and were shaped by clinical factors, patient expectations, trust, and practical constraints. Practice staff already influenced UTI management, both directly through triage, testing, and counselling and indirectly through practice routines and care pathways, while GPs differed in the degree of professional autonomy they considered appropriate. Pharmacy-based care was often only partly visible to GPs, with experiences varying according to local relationships and professional roles. Discussion The findings suggest that antibiotic-sparing UTI management extends beyond the GP prescribing decision and is shaped across the broader care pathway. Clearer professional roles, appropriate training, and feasible communication structures may support more coordinated care and antimicrobial stewardship in primary care.
n4d63e7bf5ff1: Offline reinforcement learning enables policy learning from static datasets without online exploration, making it particularly suitable for robotic control under safety and data constraints. Decision Transformer recasts offline reinforcement learning as conditional sequence modeling. Extending it to heterogeneous multi-task settings is challenging because task representations and dynamics differ, while joint training can suffer from destructive gradient interference. To address these challenges, we present HeteroGrad-DT, an integrated framework that employs task-specific tokenizers and decoupled prediction heads to retain task-native input and output dimensionality at the model interfaces while learning a shared sequence backbone. It further introduces a Gradient Flow Transformer that periodically coordinates cross-task updates using fixed-dimensional task statistics, compact summaries of shared-backbone gradients accumulated within the current synchronization interval, and an alignment-based coordination objective, rather than relying only on stepwise projection or static regularization. Experiments on the DeepMind Control Suite with up to 30 tasks show that HeteroGrad-DT improves average normalized return over representative multi-task methods. In the 30-task setting, it achieves a 32.3% relative improvement over standard training with a shared backbone and an 8.6% gain over a representative gradient-conflict mitigation baseline using the same task-aware interfaces. Ablation, mechanism, and sensitivity analyses further support complementary benefits from task-aware interfaces and gradient coordination in the evaluated settings.
n6be6994d648e: Whole slide images (WSIs) are characterized by extremely high resolution and usually lack fine-grained annotations, making multiple instance learning (MIL) the dominant paradigm for weakly supervised WSI classification. Although existing MIL methods have achieved substantial progress in feature extraction and instance aggregation, most of them overlook the influence of confounding factors, thereby learning spurious associations that impair generalization performance. To address this issue, we develop an Instance Causal Multiple Instance Learning (ICMIL) framework for WSI classification, which aims to reduce the model’s reliance on potentially spurious instance-level associations. Specifically, unlike conventional likelihood-based strategies, the proposed method introduces a backdoor-adjustment-inspired prototype module during instance aggregation, where clustered prototypes are used as proxy contextual patterns to mitigate the influence of potential confounding cues. We conduct extensive experiments on two publicly available WSI datasets, Camelyon16 and TCGA-NSCLC. The results demonstrate that the proposed ICMIL framework achieves competitive performance and generally improves existing baselines, while also exhibiting a plug-and-play property.
n80654ce500d8: Introduction Intimate partner violence is a major global public health concern and a serious human rights violation, involving physical, sexual, and psychological abuse within intimate relationships. Worldwide, about one in three women experiences intimate partner violence during their lifetime. Accordingly, this study aims to estimate the overall prevalence and identify the key predictors of intimate partner violence in Ethiopia. Methods A comprehensive systematic search was carried out in PubMed, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and African Journals Online to identify relevant systematic reviews and meta-analyses on the prevalence and predictors of intimate partner violence against women in Ethiopia. The methodological quality of the included studies was assessed using the AMSTAR-2. A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted using STATA version 18 to generate pooled estimates. Results This umbrella review synthesized evidence from six systematic reviews and meta-analyses comprising 80 primary studies involving 43,785 women. The overall prevalence of intimate partner violence was 35% (95% CI: 28–42%), with substantial heterogeneity across reviews (I2 = 83.48%). It also revealed a prevalence of 32% (95% CI: 26–37%) among pregnant women and 33% (95% CI: 25–40%) during the COVID-19 pandemic. The prevalence of specific forms of violence was estimated at 18% (95% CI: 14–22%) for sexual violence, 19% (95% CI: 15–23%) for physical violence, and 27% (95% CI: 23–31%) for psychological violence. Key predictors of IPV included both partners’ and women’s educational status, partner alcohol consumption, women’s decision-making power, substance use, and income loss during the COVID-19 pandemic, with all associations found to be statistically significant. Conclusion This umbrella review shows that intimate partner violence remains a major public health issue in Ethiopia, affecting over one-third of women. Strengthening policy implementation and expanding survivor-centered services are essential to reduce IPV and advance Sustainable Development Goal 5.
n14eff5f69a13: by Svala H. Mahmood, Iman H. F. Alnaqshabandy Uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC) presents a significant therapeutic challenge due to increasing multidrug resistance (MDR). While acquired resistance mechanisms are well-documented, the genetic variability of intrinsic efflux pumps like EmrD remains less characterized. This study investigated the genomic diversity and structural conservation of the EmrD transporter in ten clinical MDR isolates from the Kurdistan Region, Iraq. Isolates were screened for the emrD and β-lactamase genes, followed by emrD sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, and in silico protein modeling. Results confirmed the universal presence of emrD alongside multiple resistance genes. Phylogenetic analysis identified notable local genetic diversity, including a highly divergent lineage (DUH 11). Protein modeling mapped non-synonymous substitutions to transmembrane helices 6 and 12, regions critical for the “rocker-switch” conformational changes required for substrate translocation. These findings suggest that while EmrD is a stable component of the MDR machinery, localized genomic divergence may potentially influence efflux efficiency among clinical lineages, warranting future functional validation.
n48ed23ac4398: A process-based view on robust changes in characteristics of the tropical circulation under warming, the intensification of the strongest updrafts and the contraction of the deep-convective ascent area, is presented. The increase in low-level moisture under warming, directly linked to the Clausius–Clapeyron relation, and a positive feedback of latent heating on the dynamics in organized tropical convective systems drives the intensification of the strongest updrafts. Two key sets of negative feedback explain the contraction of the deep-convective ascent area. Increased latent heating in deep-convective ascent areas affects the dry-static stability of the atmosphere and the atmospheric circulation. In addition, the increased latent heating linked to the low-level moisture increase causes enhanced convergence in the deep-convective areas which leads to its dynamic contraction—a process one could call the moisture-dynamical feedback. The changes in the two aspects are related in that both are caused by increased low-level moisture content and subsequent changes in moist processes and moisture dynamics. The formulated moisture-dynamical perspective contrasts with, but does not contradict, an energy balance interpretation of the changes in tropical circulation characteristics in which varying radiative fluxes are attributed an explanatory role.
n5c8df86369db: The acute phase response is a component of innate immunity that helps fight infections. Understanding variation in this response could be critical in bats, which can be asymptomatic hosts of pathogens that cause disease in other animals. Although bats are most famously tolerant of some viruses, research on the bat acute phase response has focused predominantly on bacterial antigens. To improve understanding of bat viral responses, we challenged wild Seba's short-tailed bats (Carollia perspicillata) with a viral mimic (polyinosinic:polycytidylic acid (polyI:C)). We injected nine bats subcutaneously with 2 mg kg−1 of polyI:C (n = 3), 5 mg kg−1 of polyI:C (n = 3) or phosphate buffered saline (n = 3). Over the next 24 hours, we measured body temperature hourly and collected body mass and blood smears for leucocyte counts every 4 hours. Regardless of dose, polyI:C-challenged bats had higher body temperatures compared to control bats but did not exhibit leucocytosis or reduced body mass. These preliminary findings improve understanding of how wild bats physiologically respond to viral challenges. Moreover, in showing that as little as 2 mg kg−1 of polyI:C can induce a febrile response, our study provides a framework to facilitate future investigations into causes and consequences of wild bat viral responses.
ne39a66b20d00: In this paper, we study the absorption and fixation times for evolutionary processes on graphs, with relative fitness r>0, under different updating rules. While in the Moran process a single neighbour is randomly chosen to be replaced, in proliferation processes, other neighbours can be replaced using Bernoulli or binomial draws depending on 0<p≤1. There is a critical value pc such that the proliferation is advantageous or disadvantageous in terms of fixation probability depending on whether p>pc or p<pc. We clarify the role of symmetries for computing the fixation time in the Moran process. We show that the Maruyama–Kimura symmetry depends on the graph structure induced in each state, implying asymmetry for all graphs except cliques and cycles. There is a fitness value, not necessarily 1, beyond which the fixation time decreases monotonically. We apply Harris’s graphical method to prove that the fixation time decreases monotonically depending on p. Thus, there exists another value pt for which the proliferation is advantageous or disadvantageous in terms of time. However, at the critical level p=pc, the proliferation is highly advantageous when r tends to infinity.
nc77023bf3f8b: Quantitative image analysis is central to understanding microbial growth, morphology and spatial organization. However, conventional metrics such as mean intensity or object count often do not capture the complex structural heterogeneity and patterning characteristic of microbial colonies and biofilms. To address this limitation, analysis of biofilm complexity in 3D (ABC3D), an open-source Python framework for automated extraction of fractal, textural and statistical descriptors from volumetric microscopy images, is reported. ABC3D computes a set of parameters including fractal dimension, lacunarity, entropy, grey-level co-occurrence matrix features and relative wavelet sub-band energies from three-dimensional image datasets. ABC3D is demonstrated in Escherichia coli macrocolony biofilms, where the first two principal components captured 75.5% of architectural variance. Nutrient environment, genetic background and their interaction significantly influenced biofilm architecture, indicating that structural responses to nutrient conditions are strain-dependent. Analysis of individual parameters revealed coordinated changes in fractal, textural and spatial-frequency features rather than uniform changes in a single measure of complexity. ABC3D provides researchers with an accessible, quantitative approach to assessing biofilm morphology in microscopy datasets.
ne17021238e10: Changing their behaviour is animals' first line of defence in response to environmental disturbance. However, changes in behaviour towards social group members and mutualistic partners can also lead to reduced fitness and resilience. Here, we use clown anemonefish, Amphiprion percula, to understand how disturbances alter social and mutualistic behaviours directly and indirectly via degraded mutualistic partners. We measured fish behaviour from video recordings made during a marine heatwave in Kimbe Bay, Papua New Guinea. Since some of the hosting anemones bleached, lost symbiotic algae, and others did not, we were able to estimate the effects of heat stress separate from the indirect effects through stressed mutualistic partners. Neither stressor significantly impacted activity levels or interactions with the mutualistic partner, which made up a high proportion of behaviours throughout. However, bleaching did increase aggression between group members and defensive behaviours. Our results provide an example of behavioural plasticity in response to environmental disturbance where different behaviours were adjusted to the stressor itself or to the changing habitat. We show that some species will prioritize interactions with mutualistic partners, while their social cohesion is weakened.
n3482036dae0c: N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor antagonists are used to model schizophrenia-related phenotypes, but behavioural responses to repeated ketamine exposure in zebrafish remain poorly characterized. Three independent experiments were conducted to evaluate the acute, repeated and sustained behavioural effects of ketamine in adult zebrafish. In Experiment I, fish received 10, 20 or 40 mg l−1 ketamine daily for 5 days and were tested in the social preference test (SPT) and open tank test (OTT) on days 1, 5 and 7, with re-exposure on day 7 after a 48 h washout. Experiments II and III assessed whether behavioural changes persisted following 5- or 14-day exposure, with testing 48 h after the final treatment. Ketamine reduced social interaction and increased locomotor activity in the SPT on all days and increased rotational behaviour in the OTT on days 1 and 5. Measured responses did not progressively increase across test sessions, and most outcomes did not differ from controls 48 h after the final exposure in Experiments II and III. The results characterize the acute, concentration-dependent behavioural profile of ketamine in adult zebrafish and define the temporal window over which it is detectable. These findings differ from rodent reports of sustained effects and motivate further investigation across species.
n9130a9f5a62c: A recent study comparing UK egg production systems concluded that the current (‘business-as-usual’) UK egg production system consisting of a mix of cage and non-cage systems minimizes environmental impacts, requires fewer laying hens and results in lower mortality than alternative cage-free scenarios. While the objective of evaluating environmental and welfare consequences of production system changes is important, I argue that these conclusions are not sufficiently supported by the methodology employed. The analysis relies on life cycle inventory and mortality data generated around 2010 to represent the UK industry in 2022, despite substantial advances in genetics, nutrition, housing, flock health and management over the intervening period. More importantly, it disregards the uncertainty associated with the original environmental and production datasets, treating inherently variable biological systems as deterministic. This omission is compounded by scaling farm-level point estimates to national production, thereby magnifying apparent differences between scenarios without quantifying their statistical significance. I contend that robust policy recommendations regarding transitions between egg production systems require analyses based on contemporary production data, explicit propagation of uncertainty and integrated evaluation of environmental sustainability and animal welfare.
n418ad903409d: Population connectivity influences genetic diversity by facilitating exchange among populations. For enteric parasites, connectivity depends on host contact and environmentally mediated transmission, suggesting that disruptions to human movement could reduce diversity within infections. The COVID-19 pandemic provided a natural experiment to test this prediction. We used high-throughput gp60 metabarcoding to compare within-host amplicon sequence variant (ASVs) richness, diversity and composition before and after the pandemic in three human-infecting Cryptosporidium species with contrasting transmission ecologies: anthroponotic Cryptosporidium hominis, zoonotic Cryptosporidium parvum and wildlife-associated Cryptosporidium cuniculus. Primary analyses excluded 26 epidemiologically linked C. hominis infections from a 2023 outbreak; sensitivity analyses included these samples. Post-COVID, C. hominis showed significantly lower Shannon, Simpson and inverse-Simpson diversity, 63% fewer detectable ASVs and altered ASV composition. Cryptosporidium parvum showed compositional differences but no significant reduction in diversity or richness, whereas C. cuniculus showed no clear temporal change. Including outbreak-associated C. hominis samples attenuated diversity reductions but retained significant declines in Shannon diversity, Simpson diversity, ASV richness and composition. These findings are consistent with reduced parasite connectivity following disruption of predominantly human-associated transmission and indicate that major changes in transmission conditions can rapidly reshape the genetic diversity maintained within parasite infections.
n2c813ff68afc: The Tasmanian devil (Sarcophilus harrisii) population has undergone a major decline in the wild owing to the epidemics of two transmissible cancers known as devil facial tumour 1 (DFT1) and devil facial tumour 2 (DFT2). Understanding the distribution and prevalence of DFT1 and DFT2 is challenging as they can only be detected in field conditions when tumours are large enough to be visually observed. This impedes our ability to understand how the devil population is evolving in response to the tumours. PCR-based diagnostics are available, but the technique is not field-applicable. To overcome these hurdles, we developed an ultrasensitive and field-deployable rapid diagnostic tool. We used a technique called specific high-sensitivity enzymatic reporter unlocking (SHERLOCK), which combines an isothermal nucleic acid amplification step with CRISPR-based recognition and activation of reporter probes to indicate target sequence detection. This system requires only portable laboratory equipment, making it more amenable to field conditions. The results showed that our test can detect DFT1 and DFT2 DNA within the attomolar range. We then confirmed that the test can detect DFT1 in the field using non-invasive swab samples. The SHERLOCK test can be used for more active monitoring and management approaches that are not currently possible.
n5b5c0e825355: Territoriality is a key strategy through which animals secure access to reproductive opportunities, yet in many lekking species, males differ in their investment in defending space. Breeding aggregations often include territorial residents and non-territorial floaters, raising questions about the flexibility and endocrine regulation of alternative spatial tactics. The ruff (Calidris pugnax) provides a powerful model to address these questions because males occur as three genetically determined reproductive morphs: territorial independents and two non-territorial floater morphs, satellites and faeders. Using artificial intelligence-assisted tracking in a captive colony, we quantified fine-scale space-use patterns within experimental and control leks. Our aim was to test whether male morphs adjust spatial behaviour when social opportunities arise. Independents exhibited smaller and more segregated activity areas, whereas satellites and faeders showed larger, overlapping activity areas, consistent with a floater strategy. Despite experimentally manipulating lek composition to create single-morph social environments, neither satellites nor faeders adopted territorial-like spatial behaviour. In addition, circulating concentrations of testosterone were higher in independents than faeders and satellites, but short-term variation in testosterone was not linked to changes in spatial behaviour and experimental treatment. These findings support the view that space-use tactics in ruffs represent fixed specializations rather than flexible responses to social opportunities.
n2af67b5bcfee: What is science? Scientists often assume that we share a general understanding of what science is, yet this assumption has rarely been empirically assessed. We examined scientists’ and members of the public’s agreement with a range of common conceptualizations of science, including science as a search for truth, a mirror of nature, a free marketplace of competing ideas and others. We found substantial heterogeneity in responses to these conceptualizations, with scientists disagreeing with each other more than the public does. We also found systematic differences in how the public and scientists understand science. Members of the public tended to endorse an idealized view of science, portraying it as a reliable machine for discovering objective truths through well-defined procedures. Scientists, in contrast, were more reserved in their endorsements, often emphasizing the limitations of the scientific method, contingency of scientific results and the roles of improvisation and creativity in scientific practice. This suggests that shared understanding of science cannot be taken for granted. Differences in how we understand science have implications for science practice, education and communication.
nf8ea412398da: Zoos contribute to ex situ conservation of taxa affected by habitat loss and wildlife trade, including parrots, but their success in maintaining viable populations remains unclear. This study assessed the role of zoos in the ex situ maintenance and reproduction of Brazilian parrot species over 2004–2024 using Zoological Information Management System demographic records, Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) trade data and International Union for Conservation of Nature Red List categories. Generalized linear mixed models, generalized additive models and generalized additive mixed models tested effects of population growth, threat status, sex ratio and extinction risk in relation to trade intensity. Ex situ populations showed no consistent demographic growth. Hatching rates declined over time, and per capita net population change was near zero or negative for most species, with populations often sustained by acquisitions rather than reproduction. More threatened species did not show higher reproductive success under captive management. Sex ratio was associated with population dynamics, with more favourable outcomes near balanced ratios. International trade was positively associated with extinction risk, with species at higher threat levels appearing more frequently in trade records. These findings show that captive population growth is uneven across species and highlight the need for integrated demographic, welfare, genetic and trade management to improve conservation outcomes.
n1492abef9771: This study investigates the performance of solid-state dye-sensitized solar cells (ssDSSCs) employing four hole transport layer (HTL) candidates: cadmium telluride (CdTe) and three kesterite materials—copper-barium-tin sulfide (CBTS), copper-iron-tin sulfide (CFTS) and copper-manganese-tin sulfide (CMTS). Electrical and optical parameters collected from the literature were incorporated into SCAPS-1D for device modelling. A comprehensive analysis examined the effects of HTL thickness, temperature, absorber and electron transport layer (ETL) thickness, capacitance, parasitic resistance and doping concentration on device performance. The results demonstrate that CdTe is a highly promising HTL, with the optimized fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO)/ZnO/ruthenium complex dye (N719)/CdTe/Pt heterostructure achieving a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.58%, a fill factor (FF) of 87.86%, an open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 1.106 V and a current density (JSC) of 22.21 mA cm−², exceeding previously reported values. Among kesterite-based HTLs, CBTS and CFTS exhibited notable PCEs of 16.42 and 14.80%, respectively, outperforming comparable studies. These findings indicate that CdTe, CBTS and CFTS are strong candidates for ssDSSC applications, offering enhanced efficiency and stability. Notably, CBTS emerges as a low-cost, Earth-abundant alternative with favourable band alignment and high thermal stability. This work provides valuable insights for advancing efficient and sustainable ssDSSC technologies.
n39f7ea0a671b: Triassic sauropodomorph cranial material is known primarily from Argentina, Brazil and Europe and is sparsely distributed across the phylogenetic tree. In southern Africa, only two Late Triassic taxa preserve cranial elements, Mbiresaurus and Kholumolumo, both represented by limited material. Here we describe Nyana rooiwalensis, a new early-branching sauropodomorph from the Upper Triassic lower Elliot Formation of South Africa, represented by the first well-preserved, near-complete skull to be recovered from the unit. The holotype comprises the braincase, palate, the hyoid apparatus and scleral rings, as well as associated postcranial elements. Body mass estimates predict Nyana was approximately 400 kg yet osteohistological analyses show at most two lines of arrested growth and a crenulated periosteal surface, indicating an early ontogenetic stage. These observations support the early evolution of rapid growth in Sauropodomorpha, foreshadowing the evolution of sauropod gigantism. Phylogenetic analyses place Nyana as the sister taxon to either the North American Sarahsaurus or the South African Ngwevu and is recovered as either an early-branching massopodan or nested within Massospondylidae. The exceptional preservation, early ontogenetic stage and phylogenetic position of Nyana provide critical insights into cranial evolution, postural and locomotory behaviours, body mass and growth dynamics during the early diversification of Sauropodomorpha.
n548cbe765e6e: Tidal hydrokinetic turbines offer promising opportunities for energy generation, but turbine-induced turbulence may alter fish movement, passage and habitat use. We develop an eco-hydrodynamic integration framework that maps experimentally measured fish trajectories onto turbulence-resolved large-eddy simulation fields around a vertical axis turbine. Fish behaviour is not prescribed through a behavioural model; instead, measured occupancy patterns and swimming manoeuvres are evaluated in relation to the flow field, integral length scale and estimated swimming thrust. The simulations resolve wake asymmetry, vortex shedding, shear layers and turbulence under mild and high flow conditions. Fish predominantly occupied low-turbulence regions and avoided the energetic wake and its shear layers. In some regions, fish selected relatively higher mean velocities with lower turbulence, revealing a velocity–turbulence trade-off in habitat selection. Evasive manoeuvres were frequently observed where the turbulence integral length scale approached or exceeded fish body length, while strong wake shear layers could act as hydraulic barriers to upstream passage. The results show that turbulence may reduce rotor entry while simultaneously increasing swimming effort and disrupting passage. From an engineering perspective, the framework provides a way to evaluate turbine siting, clearance, layout and operating conditions using behaviourally relevant turbulence metrics in addition to conventional performance and blade-strike criteria.
n8b6f03e89811: Sociability towards humans is an adaptive trait in free-ranging dogs (FRDs), enabling them to access resources while navigating the risky anthropogenic habitat. We investigated whether operant conditioning shapes sociability in Indian FRDs and whether learned responses generalize to an unfamiliar individual. We exposed 54 dog groups to either a positive or a threatening cue over five consecutive days, followed by tests on day 6 with an unfamiliar and then the familiar experimenter. Using Bayesian GLMMs, we analysed approach proportion, approach latency and demeanour. The threatening cue reduced approach behaviour, increased approach latency and caused a shift towards neutral responses to the familiar experimenter, with the changes occurring earlier compared with the positive cue. The positive cue reduced approach latency towards the familiar experimenter, but did not increase the proportion of approach. Towards the unfamiliar experimenter on day 6, positive-cue groups approached more often, threatening-cue groups approached more slowly than on day 1, and demeanour changes under the threatening cue were specific to the familiar experimenter. Our results suggest that FRDs adjust their behaviour primarily towards the person associated with an outcome, which may help them balance resource acquisition with risk avoidance. These insights have implications for informing management strategies to enable dog–human coexistence.
n34788027d350: Vessel strikes are a significant and growing threat to marine megafauna, yet few mitigation measures are implemented at scale owing to perceived economic costs to shipping. Here, we present a proof of concept for integrating biodiversity considerations into commercial voyage optimization, using critical aggregation sites for the endangered whale shark (Rhincodon typus) as a case study. We simulated eight port-to-port voyages for two vessel classes—a crude oil tanker and a container ship—under three routing scenarios: baseline optimization, speed reduction to 10 kts within core habitats and complete avoidance of these areas. Across routes, fuel-use changes ranged from −0.13% to 9.65%, with minimal impacts (less than 1%) for most long-distance voyages. Results indicate that speed reduction is the more efficient mitigation for short voyages, while area avoidance is preferable for longer voyages, with impacts varying by vessel type and operational constraints. Incorporating dynamic, species-specific habitat layers into voyage planning could enable targeted vessel strike mitigation with negligible disruption to global trade. Adoption of such measures, supported by improved data pipelines, dynamic forecasting and integration into regulatory and incentive frameworks, offers a scalable pathway to align biodiversity conservation with decarbonization goals in the maritime sector.
n575ea030f0eb: Social media platforms enable both gender equality and social inclusion (GESI) advocacy and GESI violations, such as hate speech and harassment. Challenging such violations through social correction by active users is essential, yet little is known about whether users accurately perceive others' attitudes towards this behaviour across cultural contexts. This cross-sectional study, based on an online survey of 325 UK and 312 Arab participants, examines self-reported attitudes and perceptions of others' attitudes towards three barriers to social correction: Relationship Consequences, Negative Impact on others and Futility, using linear mixed modelling. Findings indicate a discrepancy between self-reported attitudes and perceptions of others' attitudes, indicating a misperception. In the UK sample, misperceptions relate to Relationship Consequences and Futility, with participants expecting greater relational costs and less behavioural change when challenging others than when being challenged themselves. In the Arab GCC sample, participants perceived the challenged person as more negatively affected than they believed they themselves would be, though this pattern was less consistent across individual measures. These findings suggest that integrating social norm nudges into social media design could correct misperceived norms and empower users to challenge GESI violations. Limitations include sample representativeness and self-reported data; future research should use broader samples and qualitative methods.
na58123b28395: Social insects rely on multiple defence mechanisms to limit pathogen transmission within colonies. Prophylactic sanitary behaviours are performed in the absence of immediate pathogenic threats and contribute to routine disease prevention. Among these behaviours, grooming and necrophoresis help manage potentially harmful biological material, but how their expression relates to variation in pathogen susceptibility among colonies remains poorly understood. We investigated the relationship between susceptibility to the entomopathogenic fungus Beauveria bassiana and the expression of prophylactic grooming and necrophoresis in the ant Lasius flavus. We found strong and consistent intercolonial differences in pathogen susceptibility, as well as marked variation in the expression of prophylactic sanitary behaviours. None of the grooming behaviours examined were associated with pathogen susceptibility. However, more pathogen-susceptible colonies tended to remove corpses more rapidly during the early phase of necrophoresis. This pattern is consistent with a possible compensatory relationship among defence components, but may also arise from demographic and organizational differences among colonies, as worker age structure and task allocation can influence both susceptibility to infection and corpse removal behaviour. Overall, our results reveal substantial intercolonial variation in multiple components of disease defence but provide little support for a compensatory relationship between pathogen susceptibility and prophylactic sanitary behaviour.
nd357debf20b9: Ca2+-release activated Ca2+ (CRAC) channels, formed by stromal interaction molecule (STIM) and Orai proteins, mediate store-operated Ca2+ entry and are implicated in autoimmune diseases, acute pancreatitis and cancer. Some small molecule inhibitors of these channels such as BTP2, Pyr6, Synta66 and GSK-7975A, are widely used as experimental tools, yet their precise mechanisms of action remain incompletely understood. Using whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology in rat basophilic leukaemia (RBL-1) cells, we determined whether each of these inhibitors acts from the extracellular or intracellular side of the plasma membrane. We found that BTP2 and GSK-7975A could suppress CRAC currents only when applied extracellularly, whereas Pyr6 and Synta66 were equally effective from either side. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations using a rat Orai1 channel model identified plausible extracellular binding sites for all four inhibitors and additional putative intracellular binding sites for Pyr6 and Synta66. These predicted sites are located near regions that are likely to influence pore geometry and channel gating. Our findings suggest that, despite considerable structural similarity, these popular CRAC channel inhibitors exhibit mechanistically distinct interactions with Orai1, with important implications for their use as research tools and for future CRAC channel drug discovery.
nef4c6e5ba71e: Health stories in the media often contain relative risks, for example, ‘Eating bacon increases your risk of colorectal cancer by 20%’. While the reported changes in risk may be accurate, they do not allow the reader to know the relevant absolute risks (i.e. their chances of developing cancer if they do, or do not, eat bacon). We investigated what people infer the absolute risks to be when they are only given relative risks. Visitors to the British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) news website read a story about the protective effects of mushroom consumption against mild cognitive impairment. Participants either saw the change in risk presented in relative format (50% decrease) or absolute format (from 19 per 100 to 9 per 100). Over 1000 people took part in the study and their data were analysed according to a pre-registered plan. We found that the median estimates of the absolute risks were correct even when participants only saw relative information, indicative of a ‘wisdom of the crowd’ effect. However, the relative format led people to have much larger errors in their estimates of the true risks when compared to the absolute format. Furthermore, the absolute format did not reduce participants' self-reported comprehension or interest in the story.
n5b32caf527b7: Duck-billed dinosaurs evolved complex cornified oral structures whose soft-tissue biology remains poorly understood. Here we investigate the rostral anatomy of the hadrosauroid Tethyshadros insularis using gross morphology and micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) data, focusing on the premaxillae and predentary. Structures previously interpreted as anomalous ‘spiked’ beak ornamentation are reinterpreted as osteological correlates of an extensive neurovascular network. Circumflex vessels, palatine and narial circulation and a median premaxillary sinus supplied a hypertrophied keratinous rhamphotheca that probably exceeded the extent of the underlying bone in both size and morphological complexity. Comparative evidence indicates that marginal denticulations reflect vascular excavation and/or ossified dermal papillary structures, implying vascular and somato-sensory functions analogous to avian beaks. Mesowear marks and functional correlates support a major role in cropping abrasive, grit-laden vegetation, while the dense vascularization suggests an additional thermoregulatory function via beak–nares heat exchange. These findings re-evaluate the hadrosauroid beak as a multifunctional sensory, mechanical and thermal organ, representing a key innovation that may have underpinned the ecological expansion and gigantism of later diverging hadrosaurids.
nad4b6d2dd360: Passive acoustic monitoring offers a scalable solution for biodiversity assessment in the Neotropics, although classifying hundreds of sympatric species in complex soundscapes remains challenging. We developed a deep learning framework for large-scale avian classification by training convolutional neural networks on recordings from 667 Neotropical bird species across northern South America. EfficientNetV2L performed best, achieving 94.48% accuracy, 94.30% macro F1-score and 0.998 macro ROC-AUC. After training, we conducted a post hoc analysis of species-level F1-scores using phylogenetically informed models (phylogenetically generalized least squares (PGLS) and phylogenetic generalized linear mixed models (PGLMM)) to test morphological, ecological and geographic predictors under phylogenetic control. Broad traits explained little interspecific variation: the best-supported PGLS accounted for approximately 2.2% of the variance, whereas the null model received the strongest support among PGLMM candidates. Geographic range size showed the most consistent negative association with F1-score, while morphological and ecological predictors added little explanatory power. Performance nevertheless showed weak but significant phylogenetic signal, and frequent confusions tended to involve more closely related species. Gradient-weighted class activation mapping and Monte Carlo Dropout provided complementary descriptions of saliency and predictive uncertainty. Overall, deep learning performed effectively for regional biodiversity monitoring and provided a comparative framework for assessing how much of the variation in acoustic classification performance could be explained by broad biological predictors.
nc1471099c652: Jingophrys is a genus of Asian horned frogs known from six species with disjunct distributions in the Himalayas and Indo-Burma. By integrating evidence from molecular phylogeny, morphology and behaviour, we uncover five new species, recognize two distinct species groups, report two new country records for India and identify additional unnamed lineages. These additions constitute a seven-fold increase in the diversity of Indian Jingophrys and a more than two-fold increase for the genus overall. We also describe the first vocal repertoires of all eight Indian members, provide accounts of umbelliform tadpoles for three members and report a previously unknown snail-eating behaviour for the family Megophryidae. Present-day patterns of diversity and endemism may have been shaped by interplay between major rivers that subdivide the Eastern Himalayas from west to east and elevational range divergence at regional scales, which yields up to four congeners within a 10 km radius. The Himalayas are an overlooked and important centre of in situ diversification for frogs in the subfamily Megophryinae. Divergence timing, rapid diversification rates and biogeographical patterns across the large megophryine radiation are coincident with active Himalayan–Tibetan orogeny through the Late Oligocene and Miocene and intensification of the South Asian monsoon system starting around 10 Ma, in Late Miocene.
nb89480ff4e95: In this study, mixed matrix membranes (MMMs) consisting of a continuous polymer phase and a dispersed metal-organic framework (MOF) phase were designed to purify hydrogen from the solar water splitting process. We first identified 20 MOFs with a small pore limiting diameter of less than or equal to 3 Å to restrict the passage of larger molecules such as N2 and O2, thereby allowing the smaller H2 molecule to pass through. These MOFs were assessed for water stability, thermal stability, solvent removal stability, and to identify open-metal sites. We developed atomistic polarizable flexible force fields for these 20 MOFs and used these in molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo simulations to calculate diffusion constants and adsorption isotherms. Using these results, we selected stable MOFs with the highest permeability and ideal selectivity for hydrogen separation. We used experimental data for polymer permeability and selectivity. Finally, we used the Maxwell model to predict the permeability and ideal selectivity of each MMM. We observed that selectivity is primarily governed by polymer properties, and permeability increases by adding MOFs as the dispersed phase. Our computed results showed that MMMs have approximately a twofold reduction in required membrane area compared with pure polymers. Triptycene-based polybenzoxazole (TPBO)-1.0/ARIBOS performed the best, requiring the smallest membrane area.
n48939fcef55d: Cholinergic dysfunction is a hallmark of Alzheimer’s disease and other memory disorders. Yet, the neurophysiological mechanisms linking cholinergic signaling to memory remain poorly understood. In this study, we administered scopolamine, a muscarinic cholinergic antagonist, to neurosurgical patients with intracranial electrodes as they performed an associative recognition memory task. When scopolamine was present at encoding, we observed disruptions to hippocampal slow theta oscillations (2–4 Hz), with selective impairments to recollection-based memory. However, when scopolamine was present during retrieval alone, we observed disruptions to slow theta without impaired memory performance. These disruptions included dose-dependent reductions in theta power, theta phase reset, and encoding–retrieval pattern reinstatement. Together, our results challenge the notion that theta oscillations are necessary for memory retrieval, and instead suggest that theta universally reflects an encoding-related neural state. These findings motivate updates to current models of acetylcholine’s role in memory and may inform future therapies targeting rhythmic biomarkers of memory dysfunction.
n4344646aa4a4: Mitochondrial dysfunction and declining ATP production are common features of aging, yet whether ATP availability itself directly regulates cellular lifespan is unclear. However, the causal relationship between cellular ATP homeostasis and aging has not been established. Here, we developed a synthetic system to manipulate intracellular ATP independently of endogenous energy production by expressing a plasma membrane-targeted nucleotide transporter, NTT1, from the intracellular parasite Encephalitozoon cuniculi in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. NTT1 expression depleted intracellular ATP in the absence of extracellular ATP, whereas ATP supplementation produced robust NTT1-dependent ATP uptake, and increased intracellular ATP abundance. ATP availability strongly influenced replicative lifespan: ATP depletion shortened lifespan, whereas ATP supplementation restored and extended lifespan in NTT1-expressing cells. Unexpectedly, extracellular ATP also extended lifespan in wild-type cells that lack ATP import, revealing an NTT1-independent response to extracellular ATP. Transcriptomic analyses showed that NTT1-mediated ATP import suppresses glucose uptake, carbohydrate catabolism, mitochondrial respiration, and autophagy, whereas extracellular ATP elicits a distinct transcriptional response in wild-type cells involving metabolic, mitochondrial, and signaling pathways. Single-cell aging analyses further showed that ATP supplementation extends lifespan across distinct aging trajectories and shifts cells away from the mitochondrial dysfunction-associated aging state. Finally, experiments in cells lacking mitochondrial DNA separated these effects mechanistically: NTT1-associated lifespan phenotypes and high-ATP toxicity required functional mitochondria, whereas extracellular ATP extended lifespan in wild-type cells independently of mitochondrial respiration. Together, these findings demonstrate that ATP availability is a direct regulator of cellular aging and reveal distinct metabolic and extracellular ATP-responsive routes through which cellular energy state influences longevity.
nba11b7f76aef: Ewing sarcoma (EwS) is a fusion-driven malignancy, peaking in adolescence. Although EwS tumors are driven uniquely by EWS::FLI1 and related fusions, patient outcomes vary greatly. If and how tumor plasticity of EWS::FLI1-regulated transcriptional signatures contributes to disease progression is not known. To address this, we utilized a single-cell co-assay of RNA and chromatin accessibility (ATAC) sequencing to identify gene regulatory networks in EwS. By comprehensively characterizing regulatory elements across cell lines, we identified multiple unique modules of gene regulation. Differential usage and prevalence of these modules was evident across cell lines, associated with distinct epigenetic and transcriptomic signatures, and in specific cases, modifiable by exogenous TGF-β. When we examined primary EwS patient tumors, we observed these same regulatory modules were variably enriched both across and within tumors, highlighting the existence of intratumoral heterogeneity in gene regulatory networks. Our findings demonstrate that multiple, co-existing transcriptional programs shape the phenotypic diversity of EwS and suggest that the balance between these networks may have important implications for clinical outcomes and targeted therapy development.
nfb3c4e069e67: Local adaptation has been demonstrated in many organisms, but the traits involved and the temporal and spatial scales at which selection acts are generally unknown. We carried out a multi-year study of 200 accessions (natural inbred lines) of Swedish Arabidopsis thaliana using local field sites and a combination of common-garden experiments that measured adult survival and fecundity, and selection experiments that measured fitness over the full life cycle. We found evidence of strong and variable selection, with particular genotypes favored more than fivefold in certain years and locations. Fecundity showed evidence of classical local adaptation, with accessions generally performing better closer to their home. However, relative to other accessions, southern ones usually had the highest fecundity—but were far more sensitive to harsh winters and slug herbivory, which strongly decreased both survival and fecundity. Furthermore, accessions originally sampled on beaches had low fecundity in all common-garden experiments, but massively outperformed all other accessions in the selection experiments, presumably due to an advantage during seedling establishment associated with their very large seeds. We conclude that local adaptation in A. thaliana reflects strong temporally and spatially varying selection on multiple traits, generally involving trade-offs and different life-history strategies, making fitness difficult to predict and measure.
n961fa323122b: In threatening situations, animals exhibit a broad range of behavioral and autonomic responses. As such, a crucial adaptive response is the inhibition of pain, which facilitates relevant defensive behaviors that promote survival. Whereas the structures and mechanisms involved in fear and pain behaviors are well documented, little is known about the precise neuronal mechanisms mediating the emotional regulation of endogenous pain-suppression. Here, we used a combination of behavioral, anatomical, optogenetic, and electrophysiological approaches to investigate, in male mice, the role of somatostatin-expressing cells in the ventrolateral periaqueductal gray matter (SST+ vlPAG cells) in the control of analgesia induced during defensive states. Our data indicate that optogenetic inhibition of SST+ vlPAG cells promotes analgesia irrespective of animal defensive state. In contrast, optogenetic activation of long-range SST+ vlPAG cells that project to the rostral ventromedial medulla (RVM) abolishes the analgesia mediated by fear behavior. Together, these results identify a novel circuit mechanism composed of long-range SST+ vlPAG cells projecting to the RVM that regulate analgesia elicited during defensive states.
ne0ca8f373016: Mutations in the adenomatous polyposis coli (APC) gene are a defining feature of colorectal cancer (CRC) and impose metabolic and stress adaptation requirements that may create exploitable vulnerabilities. Prolyl hydroxylase domain (PHD) inhibitors have been explored as therapeutic agents in CRC; however, their mechanisms of action and off-target effects remain elusive. Serendipitously, we found that Molidustat, a PHD2 inhibitor, induced cell death in human APC-mutant CRC cells. Ablation of PHD2 alone did not affect cell viability, suggesting an off-target mechanism. Using thermal proteome profiling and chemical proteomics, we identify glutathione S-transferase P1 (GSTP1) as a previously unrecognised off-target of Molidustat and demonstrate direct inhibition of its enzymatic activity. Genetic ablation of PHD2 alone did not phenocopy the cytotoxic effects of Molidustat, whereas combined loss of PHD2 and GSTP1 induced synergistic proteomic changes associated with cell-cycle suppression and apoptotic signalling. Integrated proteomic and metabolomic analyses further revealed energetic and metabolic perturbations specific to simultaneous GSTP1 and PHD2 loss. Consistent with these findings, APC-mutant mouse organoids displayed selective sensitivity to Molidustat that was not reproduced by hydroxylase inhibition alone, supporting a synthetic lethal interaction between GSTP1 and PHD2 in APC-mutant contexts. Together, these results identify a functional interaction between GSTP1 and PHD2 in a subset of CRC and suggest that off-target engagement of GSTP1 contributes to the anti-tumour activity of Molidustat.
nb794c330c37a: Sensory neurons are traditionally viewed as feature detectors that respond with an increase in firing rate to preferred stimuli while remaining unresponsive to others. Here, we identify a dual-feature encoding strategy in macaque visual cortex, wherein many neurons in areas V1 and V4 are selectively tuned to two distinct visual features—one that enhances and one that suppresses activity—around an elevated baseline firing rate. By combining neuronal recordings with functional digital twin models—deep learning-based predictive models of biological neurons—we were able to systematically identify each neuron’s preferred and non-preferred features. These feature pairs served as anchors for a continuous, low-dimensional axis in natural image similarity space, along which neuronal activity varied approximately linearly. Within a single visual area, visual features that strongly or weakly activated individual neurons also had a high probability of modulating the activity of other neurons, suggesting a shared feature selectivity across the population that structures stimulus encoding. We show that this encoding strategy is conserved across species, present in both primary and lateral visual areas of mouse cortex. Dual-feature selectivity is consistent with recent anatomical evidence for feature-specific inhibitory connectivity, complementing the feature-detector principle through circuit mechanisms in which selective excitation and inhibition may together enhance the representational capacity of the neuronal population.
neada78d98c9d: High annual honey bee colony losses are associated with environmental and biological stressors, including virus infections. n125b24145100: Biologics and immune checkpoint inhibitors have transformed the treatment of autoimmune conditions and cancers. However, safety data regarding use during pregnancy are limited. n0468515ca3f7: Aldosterone has long been viewed as a master regulator of fluid and electrolyte homeostasis, acting through the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) to stimulate electrogenic Na + transport via the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) in the distal nephron. The model holds that the key regulatory step for K + secretion involves a cell-autonomous mechanism through which local interstitial [K + ] stimulates mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2)-dependent phosphorylation of the ENaC regulatory serum- and glucocorticoid-induced kinase 1 (SGK1); the K+-sensing kinase augments this phosphorylation by serving as a scaffold to enhance the physical interaction of mTORC2 with SGK1. Aldosterone acts further downstream to stimulate ENaC primarily in the late CNT and cortical collecting duct, in which ROMK apical expression is relatively low and Na + -Cl − reabsorption is favored. n02ffad94b8a7: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) is an incretin to regulate glycemia, activates peripheral and central neural pathways to control appetite, and inhibits upper gut transit to reduce food intake. Managing upper GI complications of GLP-1RA therapy includes diet modifications, antiemetic medications, and treatments that stimulate gastric emptying. Newer agents in testing include nonpeptide GLP-1RAs and GLP-1RAs acting in concert with GIP, glucagon, or other receptor-mediated pathways.
n0b134ceca0f5: The early animal communities of the Ediacaran (∼580–539 Mya) provide novel insights into how the modern biosphere operates by recording the initial ecological framework from which ecological interactions first built up. These Ediacaran communities do not have direct counterparts because they are soft-bodied, largely heterotrophic, and predator free. However, the exceptional preservation of immobile, benthic Ediacaran animals enables the resolution of their community dynamics to similar levels to those of extant benthic systems. While many of the key processes shaping the modern benthos were present in early benthic communities, the diversity of ecological interactions within communities, and the variability of these interactions through time and space, was notably simpler than that found today. In the Ediacaran, ecosystem dynamics and complexity started with reproduction and dispersal, with adaptations and responses to the environment a secondary effect, followed by direct biotic interactions. As these biotic interactions became dominant, coevolution established a tangled bank of complexity.
na60b89a039f6: Classical ecosystem theory depicts biological nitrogen fixation (BNF) as a mechanism that replenishes disturbance-driven nitrogen (N) losses, thereby alleviating N limitation and facilitating ecosystem recovery. Focusing on forests, we find evidence that disturbance effects on BNF range from net positive to net negative and that current BNF fluxes have a limited capacity to replenish N losses if disturbances become more severe and frequent, or if they create conditions that suppress or constrain BNF. The subsequent effects of BNF on ecosystem recovery also vary. N-fixing trees and shrubs can have positive to negative effects on the recovery of carbon stocks, and under novel disturbance regimes they may alter, and even impede, forest succession. We present an updated view of BNF–recovery relationships in forest ecosystems undergoing global environmental change.
n99330c51e851: Pollen-rewarding plants face a fundamental tension: Pollen serves simultaneously as the male gametophyte and pollinator reward. We find that this reward strategy is unevenly distributed among plant families, that the resource costs of pollen rewards remain poorly characterized, and that this reward strategy may influence plant sexual-system evolution. We offer hypotheses regarding the evolution and maintenance of the pollen-reward strategy and examine the ecological and evolutionary consequences associated with its expression. We suggest that floral rewards are not isolated traits, but key elements of plant reproductive strategies, and that this perspective allows comparison among strategies and can advance our understanding of the evolutionary ecology of plant reproduction.

n3db3869c5a76: The visual system can flexibly adjust attentional deployment to match task demands, but whether observers can proactively modulate the spatial scope of attention based on expectations about upcoming search difficulty remains unclear. According to the zoom lens model, attention can narrow or broaden its spatial extent, with narrower focus enhancing processing efficiency, a mechanism that would benefit target discrimination in crowded displays. We tested whether observers adjust attentional scope when expecting sparse versus dense search arrays by combining spatial cueing with block-wise manipulations of display density expectations. Participants performed a visual search task in which endogenous cues predicted target location, while blocks predominantly contained either sparse (1 target, 3 distractors) or dense (1 target, 7 distractors) displays. We applied inverted encoding models to broadband EEG data to reconstruct spatial channel tuning functions, enabling precise characterization of both the locus and breadth of attentional deployment. Behaviorally, expecting difficult searches selectively improved accuracy at cued locations without costs elsewhere. Consistent with this selective benefit, neural measurements revealed that expectancy enhanced the amplitude of spatially selective responses at the attended location but did not alter tuning width. These findings demonstrate that expectations about search difficulty modulate attention through gain-based signal enhancement rather than adjustments to spatial scope, revealing that preparatory attentional control operates via amplitude modulation within a stable spatial focus. This mechanism complements reactive attentional adjustments and provides an efficient means for the visual system to optimize processing under predictable task demands.
nd702f2f76044: Chromosomal inversions are an important class of genetic variation that link multiple alleles together into a single inherited block that can have important effects on fitness. To study the role of large inversions in the massive evolutionary radiation of Lake Malawi cichlids, we used long-read technologies to identify four single and two tandem inversions that span half of each respective chromosome, and which together encompass over 10% of the genome. Each inversion is fixed in one of the two states within the seven major ecogroups, suggesting they played a role in the separation of the major lake lineages into specific lake habitats. One exception is within the benthic sub-radiation, where both inverted and non-inverted alleles continue to segregate within the group. The evolutionary histories of three of the six inversions suggest they transferred from the pelagic Diplotaxodon group into benthic ancestors at the time the benthic sub-radiation was seeded. The remaining three inversions are found in a subset of benthic species living in deep waters. We show that some of these inversions are linked to XY sex-determination systems but are also likely limited to a subset of total lake species. Our work suggests that inversions have been under both sexual and natural selection in Lake Malawi cichlids and that they will be important to understanding how this adaptive radiation evolved.
nb81a75e81f0b: Male Drosophila courtship behavior is a key model for studying temporal decision-making. While courtship index (CI) is widely used to quantify mating activity, other timing metrics like courtship latency, copulation latency (CL), and mating duration (MD) remain understudied. Traditional methods for quantifying these behaviors are often labor-intensive and prone to human error. In this study, we present a protocol combining a modular chamber system and automated software (DrosoMating) to quantify six key timing metrics during male courtship. Our image-based video analysis enables precise identification of courtship and copulation events, as well as quantification of their timing and duration under controlled conditions. Validation shows <0.05% error rates and 98–99% agreement with manual scoring for CL, CI, and MD. The protocol supports genetic and neural circuit manipulations, detecting subtle genetic, social, and environmental behavioral variations. By minimizing manual effort and standardizing data collection, this approach facilitates scalable, reproducible studies on adaptive trade-offs, learning, and neural mechanisms in mating behavior. This method streamlines timing analysis in male courtship, offering reproducible metrics for behavioral genetics.
n7c62b94c98b9: Epithelial cells undergo epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) during migration and regain their epithelial phenotype in the post-migration phase (mesenchymal–epithelial transition [MET]). The membrane with larger micropores failed to maintain the three-compartment epithelial structure. Live imaging revealed that KCs moved in an oscillatory manner, with actin-rich filopodia-like structures extending into and out of the 3.0 µm micropores, while the cells migrated unidirectionally into larger micropores. Piezo1 and keratin 6 were identified as negative modulators of KC entry into and exit from the 3.0 µm micropores. These results demonstrate that non-cancerous epithelial cells migrate through confined spaces in an oscillatory manner, which might contribute to the formation of a three-compartment epithelial structure that recapitulates key aspects of wound healing.
n2217a2c6fa0a: A coordinated response to stress is crucial for promoting the short- and long-term health of an organism. We find that HIF-1-mediated signaling in ADF serotonergic neurons is both necessary and sufficient for lifespan extension. Signaling through the serotonin receptor SER-7 in the GABAergic RIS interneurons is necessary in this process. Our findings also highlight the involvement of additional neural signaling molecules, including the neurotransmitters tyramine and GABA, and the neuropeptide NLP-17, in mediating longevity effects. Finally, we demonstrate that oxygen- and carbon-dioxide-sensing neurons act downstream of HIF-1 in this circuit. Together, these insights demonstrate a circuit for how genetic induction of the hypoxic response cell-nonautonomously modifies aging and suggests valuable targets for modulating aging in mammals.
n1f5bab73c569: The ability to determine how much the environment can be controlled through our actions has long been viewed as fundamental to adaptive behavior.
